about: AI content audit (2026-10-13): audience recognition 1-5, reasoning type, tile types, tile facets, issues and proposed revisions. Metadata for board construction; proposed revisions are not applied until checked (see revisions.json).

PLX-BCH-001.note: Classic TPP-enzyme list that most students recall immediately; three tiles end in 'dehydrogenase', but these are the standard names and transketolase is the discriminating member.

PLX-BCH-002.note: 'Factor II/VII/IX/X' is a numbered series and one of the most memorized lists in medicine.

revision.title: Vitamin K-dependent proteins
revision.why: Breaks the four-numeral factor series; proteins C and S are definitely gamma-carboxylated vitamin K-dependent proteins, and the reviewer note already flags them.
revision.changes: Title broadened from clotting factors to vitamin K-dependent proteins; Factor II written as Prothrombin; Factor VII and Factor X replaced by Protein C and Protein S.

PLX-BCH-003.note: COLA is a classic mnemonic, and 'Cystine' echoes the title word 'cystinuria'.

PLX-BCH-004.note: Well-known four-branch diagram; needs little thought but tiles are plausible members of other metabolite groups.

PLX-BCH-005.note: Standard recall list of irreversible bypass enzymes; quick for most students.

PLX-BCH-006.note: Classic aldose-reductase list; tiles overlap strongly with diabetic microvascular complication sites, which is the intended competitor.

PLX-BCH-007.note: Numbered 'Type _ collagen' series sorts with no reasoning; it cannot be fixed by swapping one or two tiles and needs a rebuild (e.g., OI, Stickler syndrome, vascular EDS, classical EDS as 'disorders of fibrillar collagen genes').

PLX-BCH-008.note: ADEK is the most familiar vitamin list, and the 'Vitamin _' format reveals the set.

revision.why: Removes the shared 'Vitamin' stem and letter series using standard chemical names of each vitamin, so players must recall the identity of each compound.
revision.changes: Vitamin A -> Retinol, Vitamin D -> Cholecalciferol (D3), Vitamin E -> Tocopherol, Vitamin K -> Phylloquinone (K1).

PLX-BCH-010.note: Classic microtubule-inhibitor list, but paclitaxel and vinblastine fit equally well and players may expect them.

PLX-BCH-011.note: The 'Cu/Zn' label in tile 4 announces copper; otherwise the set needs genuine recall.

revision.why: Removes the 'Cu' chemical symbol that leaks the title while keeping the same specific enzyme (SOD1 is the cytosolic Cu/Zn isoform).

PLX-BCH-012.note: 'NADPH oxidase' contains the title word and gives the link away; the rest requires recalling NADPH-consuming reactions.

revision.why: Removes the title leak while naming the same enzyme by its standard alternate name (phagocyte oxidase, NOX2).

PLX-BCH-013.note: All four end in 'deficiency' and homocysteine is the obvious hub; recognizing the remethylation vs transsulfuration split takes some thought.

PLX-BCH-014.note: All tiles share the 'deficiency' format and are recognizable urea cycle enzymes; quick for most.

PLX-BCH-015.note: Four eponymous GSDs are easy to group as GSDs; separating hepatic from muscle types only matters if BCH-040 is on the same board.

PLX-BCH-016.note: Players will sort these as neurotransmitters quickly; norepinephrine and epinephrine also depend on the PLP step upstream and may be expected.

PLX-BCH-017.note: Corkscrew hairs and perifollicular hemorrhage are textbook scurvy buzzwords, making the group instant.

PLX-BCH-018.note: Blue sclerae plus fractures is the classic OI mnemonic set ('BITE'), recognized instantly.

PLX-BCH-019.note: The '5 Ps' pattern is well known and port-wine urine anchors it, though the first three are shared with lead poisoning.

PLX-BCH-020.note: Needs specific recall and the tiles look like generic liver risk factors; estrogen use and HIV are other well-known PCT triggers players may expect.

PLX-BCH-021.note: Standard intermediate-filament stain list; neurofilaments and lamins also fit and may be expected.

PLX-BCH-022.note: Situs inversus with bronchiectasis and sinusitis is the instant Kartagener picture.

revision.why: Situs inversus is the giveaway; chronic otitis media is a very common, certain PCD manifestation, so players must discriminate PCD from cystic fibrosis rather than spot a buzzword.

PLX-BCH-023.note: Requires reasoning from mannose-6-phosphate mistargeting to tell I-cell disease from the mucopolysaccharidoses; tile 3 is long for quick reading.

PLX-BCH-024.note: 'Hexosaminidase A deficiency' names the disease's defining enzyme and makes the group instant.

revision.why: Replaces the most defining tile with a classic, certain Tay-Sachs clinical sign (hyperacusis/exaggerated startle), so players must recall the presentation and separate it from Niemann-Pick.

PLX-BCH-025.note: Angiokeratomas strongly cue Fabry; the other tiles are generic and fit many diseases.

PLX-BCH-026.note: Crumpled-paper macrophages are the Gaucher buzzword and give the group away instantly.

revision.why: Swaps the pathognomonic histology tile for a common, certain Gaucher finding (cytopenias from hypersplenism and marrow infiltration), forcing discrimination from sickle cell disease.

PLX-BCH-027.note: Globoid cells and galactocerebrosidase are strong buzzwords; optic atrophy adds a less obvious member.

PLX-BCH-028.note: 'Metachromatic' in tile 4 repeats the title; arylsulfatase A also cues the disease directly.

revision.why: Removes the title word; progressive gait disturbance/ataxia is a certain, characteristic presentation of late-infantile and juvenile MLD.

PLX-BCH-029.note: Hypermobile joints plus stretchy skin is the instant EDS picture.

revision.why: Replaces the most obvious tile with a certain classical EDS feature that overlaps scurvy and bleeding disorders, requiring discrimination.

PLX-BCH-030.note: Kinky hair names the disease; the copper labs add a Wilson look-alike only once that tile is removed.

revision.why: Removes the 'kinky hair' giveaway; hypotonia is a certain, characteristic infantile Menkes finding, leaving players to distinguish Menkes from Wilson disease.

PLX-BCH-031.note: Marfan is instant for this audience; value comes from the upward-vs-downward lens contrast if BCH-037 is placed alongside.

PLX-BCH-032.note: 'Vitamin B1/B2/B3/B5' is a numbered series that groups instantly regardless of the PDH link.

revision.why: Removes the 'Vitamin B_' series by using the standard names, so players must recall each vitamin's cofactor role rather than read a number sequence.
revision.changes: Vitamin B1 -> Thiamine, B2 -> Riboflavin, B3 -> Niacin, B5 -> Pantothenic acid.

PLX-BCH-033.note: Standard gluconeogenic substrate list; glutamine and other glucogenic amino acids also fit and lactate/alanine overlap the pyruvate-fates group.

PLX-BCH-034.note: Players will group these as counterregulatory hormones, where growth hormone is the expected fourth; the title 'in the source' is not a defensible category statement.

revision.title: Hormones that induce PEPCK expression
revision.why: 'In the source' makes the category depend on a citation rather than physiology; glucagon and epinephrine (via cAMP), glucocorticoids and thyroid hormone are all established inducers of PEPCK transcription.

PLX-BCH-035.note: The VOMIT mnemonic makes this quick for most; the essential-amino-acid and branched-chain overlaps add some discrimination.

PLX-BCH-036.note: Three tiles share the '… synthesis' format, but identifying SAM as the link requires genuine recall of methylation reactions.

PLX-BCH-037.note: Marfanoid habitus with downward lens subluxation is a well-drilled homocystinuria clue; best used alongside BCH-031 for contrast.

PLX-BCH-038.note: Classic catalase-positive CGD list; Burkholderia cepacia and Candida are other common CGD pathogens players may expect.

PLX-BCH-039.note: Tiles look like generic alcohol complications; linking them through NADH excess needs mechanistic thought and they overlap the von Gierke group.

PLX-BCH-040.note: Andersen disease is taught mainly as a hepatic GSD (and sits in BCH-015), while Tarui disease, a classic muscle GSD, is missing.

revision.why: Tarui disease (GSD VII, muscle PFK deficiency) is unambiguously a muscle GSD; replacing Andersen removes a tile usually taught as hepatic and reduces interchangeability with BCH-015.

PLX-BCH-041.note: Well-known GSD I tetrad, but it overlaps closely with the ethanol NADH-excess group, which adds real discrimination.

PLX-BCH-042.note: Classic infantile Pompe set; glycogen-filled lysosomes plus cardiomyopathy cue it quickly.

PLX-BCH-043.note: 'Second wind' is a McArdle buzzword, though the remaining tiles need some reasoning about muscle-only glycogenolysis.

PLX-BCH-044.note: Generic organ tiles must be linked by reasoning about which tissues have mitochondria and SCOT, excluding liver and RBCs.

PLX-BCH-045.note: Eruptive xanthomas with pancreatitis and creamy plasma point quickly to chylomicronemia; separating familial from acquired causes is not required.

PLX-BCH-046.note: Tendon xanthomas with high LDL is the familiar FH picture; quick for most.

PLX-BCH-047.note: Three 'Pro-' zymogens plus an A/B pair make the set mechanical to sort.

revision.why: Breaks the carboxypeptidase A/B pair; prophospholipase A2 is a pancreatic zymogen certainly activated by trypsin and links to pancreatitis pathophysiology.

PLX-BCH-048.note: The catecholamine pathway plus melanin is a drilled diagram, and thyroid hormone is a common tyrosine product players may expect.

revision.why: Removes the consecutive catecholamine trio; thyroxine is certainly derived from tyrosine residues of thyroglobulin, so players must recognize tyrosine as the shared precursor.

PLX-BCH-049.note: Musty odor cues PKU at once; the remaining tiles are generic and fit other groups.

PLX-BCH-050.note: Ochronosis and homogentisate are pathognomonic buzzwords, making the group instant.

PLX-BCH-051.note: Two 'Elevated branched-chain …' tiles plus sweet urine make MSUD instant.

revision.why: Removes the repeated 'Elevated branched-chain' stem; cerebral edema is a certain, clinically important complication of acute MSUD decompensation.

PLX-BCH-052.note: Hexagonal crystals are instantly diagnostic, and 'Increased urinary cystine' just restates the title.

revision.why: Removes the tile that restates the diagnosis. Cystine stones are a classic cause of staghorn calculi, which also makes players think of struvite.

PLX-BCH-054.note: Ringed sideroblasts anchor it quickly, but stippling and microcytosis still need separating from lead poisoning and iron deficiency.

revision.title: Classic sideroblastic anemia findings
revision.why: 'Source-described' is internal wording that does not belong in a player-facing title.

PLX-BCH-055.note: All four are also classic CYP450 inducers, and sulfonamides, fasting and progesterone/OCPs are equally classic AIP triggers players may look for.

revision.title: Precipitants of acute intermittent porphyria attacks
revision.why: 'Source-listed' is internal wording; spelling out AIP keeps the title clear.
revision.changes: Removed the 'Source-listed' prefix and expanded AIP.

PLX-BCH-056.note: Photosensitive blisters with hypertrichosis is the well-known PCT picture, so most students get it quickly.

PLX-BCH-057.note: Night blindness and Bitot spots are instant, and xerophthalmia is an umbrella term that includes the other ocular signs.

revision.title: Findings of vitamin A deficiency
revision.why: Removes the umbrella term that overlaps the other tiles and adds the classic skin finding, so the set is not purely ocular.
revision.changes: Replaced 'Xerophthalmia' with 'Follicular hyperkeratosis' and broadened the title from ocular to all findings.

PLX-BCH-058.note: Each tile is nonspecific; intracranial hypertension is the clue that points to vitamin A.

PLX-BCH-059.note: 'Rachitic' is the adjective form of rickets, so it gives away the group.

revision.why: 'Rachitic' shares its root with the title.
revision.changes: 'Rachitic rosary' became 'Costochondral beading', which means the same thing.

PLX-BCH-060.note: Two 'beriberi' tiles plus the Wernicke-Korsakoff pair make this instant.

revision.title: Manifestations of thiamine deficiency
revision.why: Names what dry and wet beriberi actually cause (neuropathy and high-output failure) instead of repeating the word 'beriberi'. The medical content is the same.
revision.changes: Dry beriberi became symmetric peripheral neuropathy, wet beriberi became high-output heart failure, and the title now says manifestations instead of syndromes.

PLX-BCH-061.note: 'Malnutrition' is vague and fits almost any deficiency, and isoniazid is a classic pellagra cause many players will look for.

revision.why: A corn-based diet is the classic dietary cause of pellagra (its niacin is poorly available) and is more specific than 'malnutrition'.

PLX-BCH-062.note: Players must separate B6 from riboflavin and B12 deficiency; sideroblastic anemia is the discriminating tile.

PLX-BCH-063.note: Methylmalonic acid with subacute combined degeneration is the textbook B12 pair.

revision.why: Three tiles now also fit folate deficiency, so players must use subacute combined degeneration to tell B12 apart. Hypersegmented neutrophils are a certain B12 deficiency finding.

PLX-BCH-064.note: Zinc is only loosely tied to 'DNA polymerase' as a family, and Mg2+ is its standard catalytic metal, so that tile is arguable.

revision.why: Alcohol dehydrogenase is an unambiguous zinc metalloenzyme, which removes the arguable DNA polymerase tile.

PLX-BCH-065.note: Each finding is nonspecific; dysgeusia with poor healing is what points to zinc.

PLX-BCH-066.note: Needs side-chain classification recall; Ser/Thr may first suggest phosphorylation sites.

PLX-BCH-067.note: Players must see why this is not 'aromatic amino acids' (isoleucine), and threonine is often listed as a fifth member.

PLX-BCH-068.note: Recalling catabolic entry points takes real effort; threonine and tryptophan also reach pyruvate but are taught less often.

PLX-BCH-069.note: Needs specific recall of entry through glutamate; the tiles more readily suggest other themes.

PLX-BCH-070.note: VLCFA oxidation with plasmalogens is the classic peroxisome list; the tiles are long for quick reading.

PLX-BCH-071.note: An ordinal series that all share 'structure' is instant; best used only as an Easy group or retired.

PLX-BCH-072.note: The aminotransferases suggest PLP, but players must recall that glycogen phosphorylase and ALA synthase also use it.

PLX-BCH-073.note: The tiles look like two pairs (catecholamines and natriuretic peptides), and glucagon, cortisol and GH are the lipolytic hormones students expect.

PLX-BCH-074.note: CPT I and CPT II plus a carnitine translocase are an instant carnitine-shuttle set.

PLX-BCH-075.note: Two HMG-CoA tiles plus beta-hydroxybutyrate point quickly to ketogenesis.

PLX-BCH-076.note: Neutral aminoaciduria all but names Hartnup disease; the other tiles also fit pellagra.

PLX-BCH-077.note: Three tiles are nonspecific for many neurometabolic disorders, and AADC deficiency is beyond standard Step 1 content, so the group borders on obscure.

PLX-BCH-078.note: Hyperammonemia with orotic acid is the classic OTC pairing, but players must rule out CPS I deficiency and orotic aciduria.

PLX-BCH-079.note: These read instantly as lysosomal storage diseases, and Hunter syndrome and ASMD (Niemann-Pick type B) also have approved ERT.

revision.title: Lysosomal storage diseases treated with enzyme replacement
revision.why: 'Described in the source' is internal wording; the new title states the shared feature directly.
revision.changes: Removed the source wording and specified lysosomal disease.

CARD-001.note: This is the textbook four-part definition of tetralogy of Fallot; use it only as an Easy group.

CARD-002.note: A well-known list; Paget disease of bone, pregnancy and sepsis are other classic high-output causes players may expect.

CARD-003.note: The shared '-dipine' suffix sorts these at a glance.

CARD-004.note: The '-olol' suffix gives away beta blockers; the real task is separating these from nonselective agents, and bisoprolol is an equally obvious missing member.

CARD-005.note: The drugs come from unrelated classes, and macrolides, fluoroquinolones and TCAs are equally classic QT prolongers players will look for.

CARD-006.note: Three class IA drugs are quickly recognized; dofetilide and ibutilide fit the title just as well as sotalol.

CARD-007.note: A familiar AF rate-control set; adenosine, which also acts at the AV node, may be expected.

CARD-008.note: Pulmonary, thyroid, liver and blue-gray skin toxicities form the classic amiodarone list and are recognized instantly.

revision.why: Without the thyroid tile, pulmonary fibrosis, liver injury and photosensitivity also suggest methotrexate, so players must reason toward amiodarone. Photosensitivity is a well-established amiodarone effect.

CARD-009.note: Cough with angioedema is the instantly recognized ACE inhibitor pair; removing cough would let ARBs fit equally, so no revision.

CARD-010.note: The repeated 'Low/High' format plus the hyperGLUC mnemonic make this quick, and hypercalcemia, the most distinctive thiazide effect, is missing.

CARD-011.note: A well-known toxic, infectious and nutritional list; Coxsackie B myocarditis and peripartum cardiomyopathy are common causes players may expect.

CARD-012.note: Infiltrative diseases are recognized quickly, but players must separate restrictive from dilated cardiomyopathy (hemochromatosis) and from constrictive pericarditis (radiation).

CARD-013.note: Asymmetric septal thickening and a murmur louder with Valsalva are the classic HOCM clues.

CARD-014.note: LV apical ballooning names Takotsubo outright.

revision.why: Normal coronaries in a stressed postmenopausal woman with an apparent infarct is a core Takotsubo diagnostic clue, and it takes reasoning rather than naming the imaging pattern.
revision.changes: Replaced 'LV apical ballooning' with 'Nonobstructive coronary arteries'.

CARD-016.note: Naming T. cruzi gives away the group, and two 'mega-' tiles reinforce it.

revision.why: Swapping the organism for Chagas's main cardiac complication means players must link the vector and GI findings to it, without the disease being named.

CARD-018.note: 'Juxtaductal aortic narrowing' is the definition of coarctation, and rib notching is a classic giveaway.

revision.why: Replaces the defining tile, which also repeats 'aortic' from the title, with a classic clinical clue to coarctation.

CARD-019.note: Three 'Exertional' tiles spell out the classic syncope, angina, dyspnea (SAD) triad.

revision.why: Removes the repeated 'Exertional' stem while keeping the same standard symptoms.
revision.changes: Exertional breathlessness became dyspnea on exertion, exertional chest pain became angina pectoris, and exertional syncope became effort syncope.

CARD-020.note: Three tiles contain 'pulse', and an early diastolic decrescendo murmur instantly signals AR.

revision.why: Uses the standard eponyms in place of descriptions that repeat 'pulse'.
revision.changes: Rapidly collapsing pulse became Corrigan pulse, and head movement with each pulse became de Musset sign.

CARD-021.note: The opening snap identifies mitral stenosis instantly.

revision.why: Replaces the giveaway sign with atrial fibrillation, a classic consequence of mitral stenosis. Players must then rely on the rumble and loud S1 to reach the diagnosis.

CARD-022.note: An apical holosystolic murmur radiating to the axilla is textbook MR, and both murmur tiles describe the same sign.

revision.why: Replaces the redundant radiation tile with mitral valve prolapse, a common, certain cause of MR, so the group mixes acute and chronic mechanisms.
revision.changes: Replaced 'Murmur radiating to axilla' with 'Mitral valve prolapse'.

CARD-023.note: The word 'Tricuspid' appears in a tile, and two tiles start with 'murmur'.

revision.why: Removes the title word and the repeated 'murmur' while keeping standard terms. Endocarditis in injection drug use is classically tricuspid.
revision.changes: Murmur louder on inspiration became Carvallo sign, and tricuspid infection in injection drug use became endocarditis in injection drug use.

CARD-024.note: Players must separate S3 from S4 settings; dilated cardiomyopathy and young athletes fit equally well.

CARD-025.note: A good discrimination pair with the S3 group: players must reason about ventricular stiffness.

CARD-027.note: Continuous murmur plus indomethacin closure names PDA instantly; 'ductal' in tile 4 echoes the title's ductus.

revision.why: Removes the word 'ductal', which echoes the title, and keeps the preterm qualifier from the reviewer notes.
revision.changes: Tile 4: 'Indomethacin-induced ductal closure' becomes 'Indomethacin closure in preterms'.

CARD-028.note: The mirror-image tiles 2 and 3 plus egg-on-string make this instant.

revision.why: Tiles 2 and 3 are a mirror pair that solve each other; balloon atrial septostomy (Rashkind) is a classic, certain TGA intervention used to improve mixing.
revision.changes: Tile 3: 'Left ventricle supplies pulmonary artery' becomes 'Balloon atrial septostomy'.

CARD-029.note: Well-known AF features; the pulmonary vein trigger tile adds some recall depth.

CARD-030.note: Sawtooth waves and CTI ablation are buzzwords for typical flutter; little reasoning needed.

CARD-031.note: Bundle of Kent plus short PR and delta wave is a textbook WPW triad.

CARD-032.note: Every tile is a first-line textbook pericarditis finding.

CARD-033.note: Requires separating constriction from restrictive cardiomyopathy and tamponade.

CARD-034.note: Beck triad plus pulsus paradoxus is a memorized set; electrical alternans is an equally classic missing member.

revision.why: Breaks the memorized Beck triad and replaces the least specific tile (hypotension) with electrical alternans, a classic tamponade finding.

CARD-035.note: Malignancy and uremia are common tamponade causes players may expect; these four share acute hemopericardium.

revision.title: Causes of acute hemopericardial tamponade
revision.why: All four act by acute bleeding into the pericardium; the narrower title excludes malignant or uremic effusions that otherwise fit equally well.
revision.changes: Title narrowed from 'Events that can cause cardiac tamponade'.

CARD-036.note: Standard pericarditis cause list; TB and SLE are common alternates.

revision.title: Recognized causes of pericarditis
revision.why: 'Source-listed' is meta wording that is meaningless to players.

CARD-037.note: Three '... rupture' tiles reveal the post-MI mechanical complication set; LV free wall rupture also overlaps CARD-035.

revision.why: Removes the repeated 'rupture' stem and the LV free wall rupture tile shared with CARD-035; post-infarction VSD is the standard name for septal rupture and LV mural thrombus is a certain post-MI complication.
revision.changes: Tile 3: 'Interventricular septal rupture' becomes 'Post-infarction VSD'; tile 4: 'LV free wall rupture' becomes 'LV mural thrombus'.

CARD-038.note: All four tiles start with 'Lead', but deciding which leads are lateral takes some recall when other lead groups are on the board.

CARD-039.note: V1-V4 is a consecutive numbered run; this is inherent to the category and can't be fixed by rewording.

CARD-040.note: 5-fluorouracil is a classic, frequently tested vasospasm drug that is missing; cocaine and amphetamines are near-duplicates.

revision.why: Amphetamines mostly duplicate cocaine (sympathomimetic stimulant); 5-FU coronary vasospasm is well established and tests a separate association.

CARD-041.note: Matches the Robbins list of SMC growth promoters, but thrombin, IFN-gamma and TGF-beta fit equally well, so the set feels arbitrary.

CARD-042.note: Classic venous stasis picture; 'venous' in tile 3 echoes the title.

revision.why: Removes the title word 'venous' from tile 3 and uses standard terms (hemosiderin staining, duplex) with the same meaning.
revision.changes: Tiles 1-4 tightened; 'Venous reflux on ultrasound' becomes 'Reflux on duplex ultrasound', 'Brown medial ankle skin' becomes 'Hemosiderin ankle staining'.

CARD-043.note: An ABI below 0.9 is an immediate PAD giveaway; the other tiles are well-known classic signs.

CARD-044.note: Well-known endocrine HTN list; acromegaly and hyperparathyroidism fit equally.

CARD-045.note: An easy fluid-loss grouping; burns add a small chance of mixing it up with distributive shock.

CARD-046.note: The ordered conduction pathway is a memorized sequence, and the bundle branches fit just as well.

CARD-047.note: The four cardiac cycle phases are a fixed set, and 'Isovolumetric'/'Ventricular' each appear twice.

CARD-048.note: Standard RAAS actions; efferent arteriolar constriction and thirst fit equally well.

CARD-049.note: PLC, IP3, DAG, PKC is a single memorized cascade that sorts itself.

CARD-050.note: A familiar mnemonic list ('S' structures), but students must tell it apart from the 1st and 3rd arch derivatives; filed under Cardiology although it is head/neck embryology.

CARD-051.note: Well-known training adaptations, all written as comparatives, which makes the group easy to spot; overlaps thematically with CARD-052.

CARD-052.note: Three tiles begin with 'Increased', which reveals the group as physiologic change statements.

revision.why: Breaks up the triple 'Increased' stem using standard terms with the same meaning.
revision.changes: Tile 1: 'Increased heart rate' becomes 'Tachycardia'; tile 2: 'Increased contractility' becomes 'Positive inotropy'.

CARD-053.note: Requires linking root dilation to AR; ankylosing spondylitis aortitis is a classic alternate, and dissection overlaps CARD-035.

CARD-054.note: The doxorubicin/daunorubicin '-rubicin' pair gives away part of the group; overlaps CARD-011.

DERM-001.note: A standard Step 1 list of epidermal residents.

DERM-002.note: Three '... junctions' tiles plus desmosomes make up the memorized junction list.

revision.why: Zonula occludens is the standard histologic name for the tight junction; this cuts the 'junctions' stem from three tiles to two.

DERM-003.note: Sandpaper rash and Pastia lines are pathognomonic textbook scarlet fever clues.

DERM-004.note: Each tile overlaps with pemphigus or TEN, so players have to put the set together to land on SSSS.

DERM-005.note: Every tile is non-specific, so the shared link has to be reasoned out.

DERM-006.note: All four tiles begin with 'Herpes'/'Herpetic', so the group sorts itself.

revision.why: Removes the 'Herpes' stem from three tiles. Primary gingivostomatitis is a classic HSV-1 syndrome, dendritic keratitis is the standard term for HSV epithelial keratitis, and temporal lobe encephalitis is the hallmark HSV-1 CNS syndrome; all certainly fit 'can cause'.
revision.changes: Herpes labialis becomes Gingivostomatitis; Herpes keratitis becomes Dendritic keratitis; Herpes encephalitis becomes Temporal lobe encephalitis.

DERM-007.note: Three tiles begin with 'Herpes zoster', which reveals the group.

revision.why: Uses standard equivalent names (shingles = herpes zoster; Ramsay Hunt syndrome = herpes zoster oticus) to cut the repeated stem from three tiles to one.
revision.changes: Tile 2: 'Herpes zoster' becomes 'Shingles'; tile 4: 'Herpes zoster oticus' becomes 'Ramsay Hunt syndrome'.

DERM-008.note: Four 'HPV' numbers sort themselves, and HPV 45/52/58 fit equally well; the format is inherent to the category.

DERM-009.note: Three tiles start with 'Verruca', so the wart group is instant.

revision.why: Uses the standard English names for verruca plana and plantaris, cutting the repeated 'Verruca' stem from three tiles to one with the same meaning.
revision.changes: Tile 2: 'Verruca plana' becomes 'Flat warts'; tile 3: 'Verruca plantaris' becomes 'Plantar warts'.

DERM-010.note: Three tiles contain 'Candid-', echoing the title, so the set is instant; no clean standard rewording exists.

revision.why: Ringworm and athlete's foot are the standard common names for tinea corporis and tinea pedis; this halves the 'Tinea' stem without changing meaning.
revision.changes: Tile 1: 'Tinea corporis' becomes 'Ringworm'; tile 3: 'Tinea pedis' becomes 'Athlete's foot'.

DERM-012.note: Malassezia plus the spaghetti-and-meatballs KOH are instant giveaways.

DERM-013.note: Rose-thorn inoculation and cigar-shaped yeast both give the answer away instantly.

DERM-014.note: A well-known mucormycosis cluster; players need to tell wide-angle from Aspergillus acute-angle branching.

DERM-015.note: Classic pemphigus vulgaris; players must separate it from the bullous pemphigoid group.

DERM-016.note: Classic pemphigoid contrast set; well known but has to be separated from pemphigus.

DERM-017.note: Celiac disease plus dapsone makes the dermatitis herpetiformis link instant.

DERM-018.note: Three granulomatous infections tempt players toward 'granulomatous infections', and strep breaks that pattern.

DERM-019.note: Tiles 1, 3 and 4 spell out the DRESS acronym (Drug Reaction, Eosinophilia, Systemic).

revision.title: DRESS syndrome associations
revision.why: Stops the tiles spelling out the acronym. Carbamazepine (an aromatic anticonvulsant) is a classic DRESS culprit and also tempts toward SJS/TEN; HHV-6 reactivation is a well-established DRESS association.
revision.changes: Tile 1: 'Delayed drug reaction' becomes 'Carbamazepine'; tile 4: 'Systemic involvement' becomes 'HHV-6 reactivation'; title changed from 'presentation' to 'associations'.

DERM-020.note: Players must recognize the type IV hypersensitivity sequence; spongiosis ties it to dermatitis.

DERM-021.note: Type 2 features also fit asthma; the filaggrin tile pins the group to atopic dermatitis.

DERM-022.note: A memorized four-factor list, and the organism name 'acnes' echoes the title.

DERM-023.note: Intertriginous nodules plus sinus tracts point quickly to hidradenitis; adalimumab adds mild ambiguity with IBD and psoriasis.

DERM-024.note: Accurate generic flushing triggers, but sunlight/UV and hot beverages are equally classic rosacea triggers players may expect.

DERM-025.note: Rhinophyma reveals rosacea immediately; the other tiles are broader.

DERM-026.note: Wickham striae and saw-tooth rete ridges are textbook lichen planus giveaways; hep C adds a little discrimination against PCT/cryoglobulinemia.

DERM-027.note: Herald patch and Christmas-tree distribution are instant pityriasis rosea identifiers.

DERM-028.note: Munro microabscesses give it away; reduced granular layer usefully contrasts with lichen planus hypergranulosis.

DERM-029.note: Psoriatic arthritis repeats the title root and, with Auspitz sign and silvery plaques, makes the group instant.

revision.why: Psoriatic arthritis leaks the title word; Koebner phenomenon is a certain, classic psoriasis association that also tempts toward lichen planus and vitiligo.

DERM-030.note: Correct, but UV exposure and actinic keratosis are the most common SCC risk factors and players will expect them; chronic wounds and burn scars overlap conceptually.

DERM-031.note: Pearly lesion with telangiectasias and palisading nuclei is the canonical BCC description.

DERM-032.note: Rapid growth plus spontaneous regression points quickly to keratoacanthoma, though the crateriform plug overlaps with SCC.

DERM-033.note: All four tiles end in 'melanoma', so the set sorts without reasoning; dropping the stem is not clean because 'lentigo maligna' alone denotes the in situ lesion.

DERM-035.note: Bartonella makes it quick; neutrophilic infiltrate and Warthin-Starry stain nicely discriminate from Kaposi sarcoma.

DERM-036.note: HHV-8 plus violaceous lesions in HIV is an instant Kaposi sarcoma identification.

DERM-037.note: Velvety dark intertriginous plaques with insulin resistance is the textbook acanthosis nigricans description.

DERM-038.note: 'Stuck-on' appearance and Leser-Trelat sign are direct seborrheic keratosis giveaways.

ENDO-001.note: All four share the '-RH' releasing-hormone format and form the canonical hypothalamic releasing-hormone list.

ENDO-002.note: The four tropic anterior pituitary hormones are a memorized set; the only discrimination is excluding GH and prolactin.

ENDO-003.note: Small cell carcinoma flags SIADH quickly; the drug list is a standard memorized set.

ENDO-005.note: Correct central DI causes, but pituitary surgery and craniopharyngioma are commoner causes players may expect; LCH is the main clue.

ENDO-006.note: Metoclopramide among antipsychotics points to D2 blockade and hyperprolactinemia; the link takes a moment beyond 'antipsychotics'.

ENDO-007.note: Correct, but Sheehan syndrome is ischemic rather than strictly structural, and pituitary adenoma (the commonest cause) is an expected missing member.

ENDO-008.note: Coarse facial growth with enlarged hands and feet is the classic acromegaly picture.

ENDO-009.note: Pegvisomant is a near-unique acromegaly clue; octreotide and cabergoline add some prolactinoma/carcinoid ambiguity.

ENDO-010.note: Requires recalling a specific mechanism shared by unrelated drugs; overlaps heavily with ENDO-011 (propranolol, PTU), so the two should not appear together.

ENDO-011.note: All four begin with 'P' (the '4 Ps' mnemonic), and 'source regimen' in the title is internal wording.

revision.title: Thyroid storm management
revision.why: Hydrocortisone is the glucocorticoid guidelines recommend in thyroid storm, so it is certainly correct and breaks the all-'P' giveaway; the title drops internal 'source' wording.
revision.changes: Replace 'Prednisolone' with 'Hydrocortisone'; retitle to 'Thyroid storm management'.

ENDO-012.note: Exophthalmos plus pretibial myxedema is instant Graves disease.

ENDO-013.note: Antithyroid antibodies with lymphoid germinal centers point quickly to Hashimoto thyroiditis.

ENDO-014.note: Painful thyroid after a viral illness is the classic de Quervain presentation.

ENDO-015.note: Good overlap with Down and Beckwith-Wiedemann syndromes, though 'umbilical protrusion' is nonstandard for the classic umbilical hernia.

revision.why: 'Umbilical hernia' is the standard term for the classic finding.

ENDO-016.note: Orphan Annie nuclei and psammoma bodies are the canonical papillary thyroid carcinoma clues.

ENDO-017.note: Capsular and vascular invasion signal follicular carcinoma versus adenoma; the translocation confirms it.

ENDO-018.note: C cells and calcitonin are an instant medullary carcinoma identification.

ENDO-019.note: Chvostek and Trousseau signs are the classic hypocalcemia pair.

ENDO-020.note: The 'stones, bones, groans, psychiatric overtones' mnemonic; 'Calcium' in the first tile echoes the title.

revision.why: Removes the word 'calcium', which repeats the title, with an exact standard synonym.

ENDO-021.note: All four tiles begin 'Increased' and three say 'renal', so the group sorts on format before physiology.

revision.why: Removes the repeated 'Increased' and 'renal' stems; title already states the actions are increases, and meaning is unchanged (PTH acts on distal convoluted tubule calcium reabsorption).
revision.changes: Drop 'Increased' from all tiles; 'Increased urinary phosphate excretion' becomes 'Phosphaturia'; 'renal calcium reabsorption' specified as distal tubule.

ENDO-022.note: Fat malabsorption is a quick link; chronic pancreatitis and cholestatic liver disease fit equally well.

ENDO-023.note: Three tiles start 'Elevated'; alkaline phosphatase is often normal in mild disease, and 'Elevated PTH' also appears verbatim in ENDO-024.

revision.why: Uses standard single terms for calcium and phosphate to break the repeated 'Elevated' format without changing meaning.
revision.changes: 'Elevated serum calcium' to 'Hypercalcemia'; 'Low serum phosphate' to 'Hypophosphatemia'.

ENDO-024.note: Requires distinguishing secondary from primary hyperparathyroidism via phosphate and calcitriol; shares 'Elevated PTH' verbatim with ENDO-023, so they should not appear together.

ENDO-025.note: CaSR and low urinary calcium give FHH away; hypercalcemia alone is broad.

ENDO-026.note: High ACTH with low aldosterone distinguishes primary from secondary disease; hyponatremia is an equally expected member.

ENDO-027.note: Purple striae with central adiposity and a dorsocervical fat pad is the textbook Cushing appearance.

ENDO-028.note: Requires reasoning from reduced effective renal perfusion; nephrotic syndrome would fit equally well.

ENDO-029.note: MEN2A/MEN2B form an obvious pair and the set is a standard memorized list.

ENDO-030.note: MYCN plus Homer Wright rosettes points quickly to neuroblastoma; VMA/HVA overlap with pheochromocytoma.

ENDO-031.note: Four '... deficiency' tiles (three '-hydroxylase') sort instantly; 3-beta-HSD deficiency fits the title equally well.

ENDO-032.note: Elevated 17-OHP identifies 21-hydroxylase deficiency; the electrolyte pattern requires mechanistic reasoning and overlaps with Addison disease.

ENDO-033.note: Must discriminate from 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency; ENDO-034 shares three identical tiles, so the two must never appear together.

ENDO-034.note: Three tiles are identical to ENDO-033, so the pair only differ by the androgen tile; 11-deoxycortisol is the diagnostic marker unique to this deficiency.

revision.why: Elevated 11-deoxycortisol is the standard diagnostic marker of 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency (it is low in 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency), removing a verbatim duplicate tile shared with ENDO-033.

ENDO-035.note: Requires reasoning through testosterone- versus DHT-dependent development and discrimination from androgen insensitivity.

ENDO-036.note: Three tiles end in 'synthesis', and the anabolic theme makes insulin obvious once GLUT4 is seen.

revision.why: Standard single-word terms reduce the repeated 'synthesis' stem with identical meaning.

ENDO-037.note: Familiar autoimmune cluster around T1DM; vitiligo, pernicious anemia and Graves disease fit equally well as associated conditions.

ENDO-038.note: Two near-identical arteriolar hyalinosis tiles pair off instantly; the efferent tile is the useful discriminator from hypertensive disease.

ENDO-039.note: Reasonable precipitant set; stroke, trauma and glucocorticoids are equally common precipitants players may expect.

ENDO-040.note: Kussmaul breathing plus fruity breath is a textbook DKA giveaway.

revision.why: Fruity breath is the most instantly recognizable DKA tile; abdominal pain is a classic, well-documented DKA presentation (correlates with acidosis severity) that forces players to connect it with the metabolic tiles.

ENDO-041.note: Three 'gli-' names plus tolbutamide are sorted by suffix alone; meglitinides also close K-ATP channels.

revision.why: Reduces the revealing 'gli-' stem from three tiles to two; chlorpropamide is a standard first-generation sulfonylurea (known for disulfiram-like reaction and SIADH) and certainly closes beta-cell K-ATP channels.

ENDO-042.note: Well-known weight-loss trio; metformin is closer to weight-neutral, and semaglutide, empagliflozin or pramlintide fit equally well.

revision.title: Glucose-lowering agents associated with weight loss
revision.why: 'Source-listed' is meta wording that does not belong in a player-facing title.

GI-001.note: Standard embryology list; proximal duodenum and gallbladder are also foregut derivatives players may expect.

GI-002.note: The four muscles of mastication are a closed, memorized set and two tiles share 'pterygoid'.

GI-003.note: Three '-glossus' tiles plus a tile containing 'tongue' make the group instant.

GI-004.note: Reactive arthritis, HIV and hematinic deficiencies also cause oral ulcers; SLE ulcers are typically painless palatal ulcers rather than true aphthae.

revision.title: Systemic diseases associated with recurrent oral ulcers
revision.why: SLE oral ulcers are classically painless mucosal ulcers, not strictly aphthous; 'oral ulcers' is accurate for all four.
revision.changes: Changed 'aphthous oral ulcers' to 'oral ulcers'; membership unchanged.

GI-005.note: Classic gingival hyperplasia list; the CCB tile is a class among single agents, which hints the drug theme.

GI-006.note: Well-known macroglossia list; Down syndrome is an equally expected member.

GI-007.note: Classic pill-esophagitis quartet; NSAIDs are an equally common culprit players may expect.

GI-008.note: Bird-beak narrowing and impaired LES relaxation are instant achalasia identifiers.

GI-009.note: Mixed mechanisms require thought; smoking, alcohol and LES-relaxing drugs fit equally well.

GI-010.note: Three tiles begin with 'Esophageal', making the grouping easy to spot.

revision.why: Removes one repeated 'Esophageal' stem; peptic stricture is the most common benign mechanical cause of esophageal narrowing and certainly fits.
revision.changes: Replaced 'Esophageal stricture' with its standard common subtype 'Peptic stricture'.

GI-013.note: Celiac B12 deficiency is a weak association (terminal ileum spared) while the most expected GI cause, ileal disease/resection, is missing.

revision.why: Terminal ileal resection definitely causes B12 deficiency (loss of the IF-B12 absorption site) and is the classic GI cause players expect; celiac is weaker for B12 and already appears in other groups in this set.

GI-014.note: Straightforward pernicious anemia cascade; achlorhydria and hypergastrinemia fit equally well.

GI-015.note: Enlarged folds and hypoalbuminemia overlap with ZES and nephrotic syndrome; foveolar hyperplasia is the key discriminator.

GI-016.note: Hypergastrinemia plus refractory ulcers points quickly to gastrinoma.

GI-017.note: All four share the '-prazole' suffix; sorting needs no medical reasoning.

GI-018.note: Requires knowing which absorption steps depend on gastric acid; generic nutrient tiles invite other groupings.

GI-019.note: Needs specific pharmacology recall; tiles also fit ketoconazole, spironolactone or trimethoprim.

GI-020.note: Requires zonal reasoning; congestive hepatopathy (right heart failure) is an equally classic zone 3 member.

GI-022.note: ATP7B and Kayser-Fleischer rings each identify Wilson disease instantly.

GI-023.note: Penicillamine and trientine point to copper chelation quickly; zinc and diet need a moment.

GI-024.note: Three 'Increased' tiles of the iron panel sort by format; the pattern must be told apart from chronic disease and deficiency.

revision.why: Removes the repeated 'Increased' stem while keeping identical meaning in standard terminology (≥45% is the usual HH screening threshold).
revision.changes: Rephrased tiles 1 to 4 to vary format.

GI-025.note: 'Bronze skin' plus diabetes is the textbook 'bronze diabetes' giveaway.

revision.why: Second/third MCP joint arthropathy is a common, definitely correct extrahepatic manifestation of hemochromatosis and requires more recall than the bronze-skin giveaway.

GI-026.note: Three 'defer-' chelators share a stem, so phlebotomy is the only tile needing thought.

GI-027.note: Generic labs with many other causes; players must reason about hepatic synthetic and metabolic roles.

GI-028.note: Well-known cirrhosis stigmata; testicular atrophy fits equally well.

GI-029.note: Varices and caput medusae make this instant, and ascites, the most expected manifestation, is absent.

revision.why: Ascites is a definite, classic manifestation of (sinusoidal) portal hypertension whose absence made the group feel arbitrary; removing esophageal varices also removes the repeated 'varices' stem and the most obvious tile.

GI-030.note: Recognizing schistosomiasis and Budd-Chiari as portal hypertension causes takes genuine recall.

GI-031.note: Crigler-Najjar type I and II form an obvious pair, and Gilbert plus Crigler-Najjar also repeat GI-033.

revision.why: Atazanavir competitively inhibits UGT1A1 and characteristically causes benign unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia; it breaks the type I/II series and reduces overlap with GI-033.

GI-032.note: Three 'jaundice' tiles and 'neonatal' in a tile give the group away; distinguishing breast milk from suboptimal-intake jaundice is the real content.

revision.why: Removes the title word 'neonatal' and the long parenthetical while keeping standard terms with identical meaning.

GI-033.note: The four hereditary hyperbilirubinemias are a classic memorized list.

GI-034.note: Fits the familiar '4 Fs'; pregnancy, female sex and Native American ancestry are equally expected.

GI-035.note: Jaundice, dark urine and pale stools is the textbook obstructive triad.

revision.why: Steatorrhea definitely results from bile acid deficiency in obstructive cholestasis and invites confusion with pancreatic causes, removing the most obvious tile.

GI-036.note: Murphy sign and HIDA nonvisualization are instant cholecystitis identifiers, and two tiles name the gallbladder.

GI-037.note: UC plus beaded ducts points quickly to PSC.

GI-039.note: Straight from the 'I GET SMASHED' mnemonic; trauma, scorpion sting and drugs fit equally well.

GI-040.note: Furosemide is a weak, circumstantial association while valproate, a classic strong culprit, is missing.

revision.why: Valproic acid has a well-established association with acute pancreatitis (boxed warning), unlike furosemide; it also removes the paired-diuretic hint.

GI-041.note: 'Hemorrhagic pancreatitis' repeats a title word and is a severe form rather than a complication.

revision.why: Hypocalcemia (fat saponification) is a definite, classic complication of acute pancreatitis and removes the title leak.

GI-042.note: Normal D-xylose requires reasoning to separate pancreatic from mucosal malabsorption.

GI-044.note: Courvoisier sign and Trousseau syndrome are well-known pancreatic cancer clues.

GI-045.note: All four end in '-oma' and gastrinoma, a common functional pancreatic NET, is an equally valid missing member.

GI-046.note: Necrolytic migratory erythema is a near-pathognomonic giveaway, though diabetes and weight loss overlap with somatostatinoma.

GI-047.note: Watery diarrhea with hypokalemia and achlorhydria is the WDHA triad, recognizable to most.

GI-048.note: Generic tiles overlap with glucagonoma and malabsorption; recognizing the somatostatin inhibitory triad requires recall.

GI-049.note: All four end in 'cells' and are the standard list of intestinal epithelial lineages, so sorting is quick; the stem cannot be dropped without nonstandard terms.

GI-051.note: Anti-tTG plus the Marsh triad is the textbook celiac picture and is identified instantly.

GI-052.note: Culture-negative endocarditis plus migratory arthralgias needs genuine recall to land on Whipple rather than rheumatic fever or other systemic infections.

GI-053.note: The MTP tile names the defect outright; acanthocytes plus low ApoB lipoproteins make the link quick.

revision.why: The MTP defect tile names the disease mechanism directly; pigmented retinopathy from fat-soluble vitamin (E/A) deficiency is a classic, certain clinical clue that requires linking the findings.
revision.changes: Replaced 'Microsomal triglyceride transfer protein (MTP) defect' with 'Retinitis pigmentosa'.

GI-054.note: Standard lead-point list, but 'Intestinal tumor' is vague and IgA vasculitis (HSP), a classic lead point, is a likely expected member.

revision.why: 'Intestinal tumor' overlaps with 'Intestinal polyp' and shares a stem; bowel-wall hematoma in IgA vasculitis is a well-established lead point and needs more reasoning.

GI-055.note: Currant-jelly stool, sausage mass and target sign are the classic intussusception triad plus imaging and are recognized instantly.

GI-056.note: Flushing, diarrhea, bronchospasm and right-sided valve disease is the memorized carcinoid syndrome list.

GI-057.note: Skip lesions, creeping fat, noncaseating granulomas and fistulas are the textbook Crohn list.

GI-058.note: Continuous rectal involvement and lead-pipe colon identify UC immediately.

GI-059.note: The first tile spells out 'IBD-associated', and primary sclerosing cholangitis is a very common expected member.

revision.why: 'Enteropathic (IBD-associated) arthritis' states the category; sacroiliitis is a standard, certain axial IBD manifestation that also tempts toward spondyloarthropathy groups.

GI-060.note: Standard appendicitis-cause list; 'Appendiceal neoplasm' repeats the title word and gives the group away.

revision.why: Removes the title-word leak; carcinoid (neuroendocrine) tumor is the classic appendiceal neoplasm and a recognized cause of luminal obstruction.

GI-061.note: 'Distal colonic aganglionosis' is essentially the definition of Hirschsprung disease.

revision.why: The aganglionosis tile names the disease; the explosive expulsion of stool on rectal exam (squirt sign) is a classic, certain bedside clue that requires recall.
revision.changes: Replaced 'Distal colonic aganglionosis' with 'Explosive stool after rectal exam'.

GI-062.note: Students sort these as hereditary CRC syndromes at once; only the AD-versus-MUTYH distinction requires thought, and 'syndrome' repeats in three tiles.

GI-063.note: Osteomas plus desmoids is the classic Gardner pairing; CHRPE is a commonly expected alternate member.

GI-064.note: Two magnesium salts side by side plus PEG and lactulose make the osmotic-laxative link instant.

revision.why: Two magnesium tiles reveal the group; sorbitol is a certain osmotic laxative and is also tempting toward sugar-alcohol or diarrhea-cause groups.

GI-065.note: All four share the -setron suffix, which sorts them without reasoning; this is structural to the category.

GI-066.note: Lateral-to-epigastric and deep-ring tiles are classic indirect-hernia clues; 'inguinal' repeats from the title.

PLEXUS-GEN-001.note: H2A/H2B/H3/H4 is a lettered/numbered series sorted on format alone; not fixable without changing the category.

PLEXUS-GEN-002.note: Paired -tecan and -poside suffixes reveal the set, and anthracyclines (doxorubicin) also inhibit topoisomerase II and fit the title equally.

revision.why: Teniposide pairs visibly with etoposide; doxorubicin is a certain topoisomerase II poison and the most common member players would expect.

PLEXUS-GEN-004.note: The four classic trinucleotide repeat disorders are a memorized list.

PLEXUS-GEN-007.note: 'Elevated urinary orotic acid' repeats the title; normal ammonia is the real discriminator from OTC deficiency.

revision.title: Hereditary UMP synthase deficiency findings
revision.why: The current title shares 'orotic' with tile 1, so the title answers the tile.
revision.changes: Retitled to name the enzyme defect; membership unchanged.

PLEXUS-GEN-008.note: Extreme photosensitivity with early skin cancers points quickly to XP.

PLEXUS-GEN-009.note: Glycosylase and AP endonuclease are the BER signature enzymes, and three tiles start with 'DNA'.

PLEXUS-GEN-010.note: 'Ataxia' and 'Telangiectasias' spell out the disease name, which also appears in the title.

revision.title: ATM deficiency clinical and laboratory clues
revision.why: Tiles 1 and 2 together give the disease name; ionizing radiation hypersensitivity is a certain hallmark of defective ATM-mediated DNA damage response, and the new title avoids repeating tile words.
revision.changes: Replaced 'Telangiectasias' with 'Ionizing radiation hypersensitivity'; retitled to 'ATM deficiency clinical and laboratory clues'.

PLEXUS-GEN-011.note: Cafe-au-lait macules pull toward NF1, so players must combine marrow failure and skeletal anomalies to reach Fanconi anemia.

PLEXUS-GEN-012.note: Butterfly rash suggests lupus, so Bloom requires combining growth deficiency and cancer risk; the rash tile is long but precise.

PLEXUS-GEN-013.note: Taq polymerase and primers identify PCR immediately.

PLEXUS-GEN-014.note: Every tile contains 'blot' (also in the title) in a paired format, so sorting needs no reasoning; better suited to a learning mode.

PLEXUS-GEN-015.note: Cafe-au-lait macules, Lisch nodules and neurofibromas are the memorized NF1 triad.

revision.why: Cafe-au-lait macules are the most reflexive NF1 cue and also overlap with the Fanconi anemia set in this chunk; axillary freckling is a certain NF1 diagnostic criterion.

PLEXUS-GEN-016.note: Hyperphagia with obesity is the reflexive Prader-Willi cue, and obesity is redundant with hyperphagia.

revision.why: Obesity duplicates hyperphagia; small hands and feet is a certain, classic Prader-Willi feature that requires recall.

PLEXUS-GEN-017.note: Inappropriate laughter is the reflexive 'happy puppet' Angelman cue.

PLEXUS-GEN-018.note: Meconium ileus plus pancreatic insufficiency points quickly to cystic fibrosis.

PLEXUS-GEN-019.note: Thick secretions plus nasal polyps point to CF fairly quickly, though primary ciliary dyskinesia is a look-alike.

PLEXUS-GEN-020.note: Dactylitis with acute chest syndrome identifies sickle cell vaso-occlusion instantly.

PLEXUS-GEN-021.note: Each tile is a well-known sickle cell association, but 'Additional' in the title depends on PLEXUS-GEN-020 and is not self-contained.

PLEXUS-GEN-022.note: Gowers sign with calf pseudohypertrophy is the instant Duchenne picture.

PLEXUS-GEN-023.note: Cataracts, frontal balding and testicular atrophy is the memorized DM1 cluster, recognized quickly by most.

PLEXUS-GEN-024.note: Macroorchidism with long face and large ears is the instant Fragile X picture.

PLEXUS-GEN-026.note: Dorsal columns plus lateral corticospinal tracts mimic B12 deficiency, so players must use spinocerebellar tracts and dorsal root ganglia to land on Friedreich ataxia.

PLEXUS-GEN-027.note: Chorea with psychiatric features points to Huntington quickly; the Early/Late qualifiers pair the motor tiles.

PLEXUS-GEN-028.note: Holoprosencephaly plus polydactyly points quickly to trisomy 13, though it must be told apart from trisomy 18.

PLEXUS-GEN-029.note: Clenched overlapping fingers and rocker-bottom feet are the reflexive trisomy 18 cues.

PLEXUS-GEN-030.note: Duodenal atresia with AVSD points quickly to Down syndrome; leukemia and hypothyroidism are also commonly expected members.

PLEXUS-GEN-031.note: Brushfield spots and single palmar crease identify Down syndrome instantly.

PLEXUS-GEN-032.note: The cat-like cry names the syndrome; without it the other three are nonspecific, so it is hard to fix by swapping.

PLEXUS-GEN-033.note: The ELN deletion tile is a genetic lesion, not a cardiovascular or metabolic association as the title states, and it names the mechanism outright.

revision.why: Makes every tile fit the title literally; peripheral pulmonary artery stenosis is a certain elastin-arteriopathy lesion in Williams syndrome.
revision.changes: Replaced 'Elastin (ELN) gene deletion' with 'Peripheral pulmonary artery stenosis'.

PLX-HEM-001.note: Three tiles share the -grel stem and ticlopidine is the known fourth; structural to the class.

PLX-HEM-003.note: XII/XI/IX/VIII is a numbered series that is sorted on format alone.

revision.title: Intrinsic-pathway components in the classic cascade
revision.why: Breaks the consecutive Roman-numeral series; prekallikrein and HMWK are certain contact-phase intrinsic-pathway components (deficiency prolongs aPTT), and the title is broadened from 'factors' to 'components'.
revision.changes: Replaced 'Factor XII' with 'Prekallikrein' and 'Factor XI' with 'High-molecular-weight kininogen'; retitled.

PLX-HEM-004.note: Mycoplasma and EBV make the cold-agglutinin link quick; CLL is classically a warm-AIHA association, which makes that tile feel loose.

revision.why: CLL is far more classically linked to warm AIHA; syphilis is a certain cause of paroxysmal cold hemoglobinuria via the cold-reactive Donath-Landsteiner antibody.

PLX-HEM-005.note: Methyldopa and penicillin are the classic drug-induced hemolysis pair; quinidine and NSAIDs are also commonly expected members.

PLX-HEM-006.note: Fava beans alone gives the group away instantly, and the vague class tiles add little reasoning.

revision.why: Fava beans is an instant giveaway; naming primaquine (the classic high-risk antimalarial) is more precise than the whole class, and nitrofurantoin is a well-established oxidant trigger (labelled for hemolysis in G6PD deficiency).
revision.changes: Fava beans -> Nitrofurantoin; Antimalarial drugs -> Primaquine

PLX-HEM-007.note: Heinz bodies plus bite cells is a textbook pairing that identifies G6PD deficiency immediately.

PLX-HEM-008.note: Spherocytes with osmotic fragility point quickly to HS; the negative DAT is the useful discriminator from warm AIHA.

PLX-HEM-009.note: PIGA and CD55/CD59 are pathognomonic textbook tiles; recognition is instant.

PLX-HEM-010.note: The classic hemolysis panel, and three tiles share the Increased/Decreased format.

revision.why: Removes the repeated Increased/Decreased format using standard equivalent terms.
revision.changes: Increased LDH -> Elevated LDH; Increased indirect bilirubin -> Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia; Decreased haptoglobin -> Low haptoglobin

PLX-HEM-011.note: TTP/HUS/DIC is the stock schistocyte list; HELLP and malignant hypertension fit equally well.

revision.why: The TTP+HUS pairing is the reflex giveaway; HELLP syndrome definitely produces schistocytes (its H is microangiopathic hemolysis) and requires more thought. Also lessens overlap with the dedicated HUS group (PLX-HEM-035).

PLX-HEM-013.note: Sickled erythrocytes echoes the title and gives it away; reticulocytosis is a count, not a smear finding (polychromasia is the smear correlate).

revision.why: Polychromasia is the smear finding that reflects reticulocytosis, making the tile accurate for a smear-findings title.

PLX-HEM-014.note: Requires linking low ATP to a glycolytic defect; the inheritance and hemolysis tiles are generic, so reasoning is needed.

PLX-HEM-016.note: Koilonychia and Plummer-Vinson are well-known iron-deficiency clues; glossitis adds mild overlap with B12/folate.

PLX-HEM-017.note: Standard chronic blood-loss causes; hookworm needs a moment but the set is familiar.

PLX-HEM-018.note: Increased hepcidin points straight to inflammation; low TIBC with preserved ferritin separates it from iron deficiency.

PLX-HEM-019.note: Wrist drop plus colic is a classic lead pairing; the word lead appears in a tile.

revision.why: Burton line is the standard eponym for the gingival lead line and removes the title word from the tile.

PLX-HEM-020.note: Two tiles end in inhibition and two contain ALA, so the heme-pathway set sorts itself.

revision.why: Lead certainly causes ringed sideroblasts (acquired sideroblastic anemia via ferrochelatase inhibition) and elevated zinc protoporphyrin; this removes the repeated inhibition/ALA stems while keeping the mechanism content.
revision.changes: Ferrochelatase inhibition -> Ringed sideroblasts; Increased urinary ALA -> Elevated zinc protoporphyrin

PLX-HEM-021.note: Requires recall beyond isoniazid; players may expect lead or copper deficiency in an acquired sideroblastic set.

PLX-HEM-023.note: A 1-to-4 gene-deletion series with alpha-thalassemia and hemoglobin repeated in tiles; cannot be fixed without reframing the connection.

PLX-HEM-024.note: Increased HbA2 is the hallmark of beta-thalassemia trait and is variable in major, so that tile is loose.

revision.why: HbA2 elevation is variable in beta-thalassemia major (its hallmark is trait); transfusional iron overload is a certain, defining association of major.

PLX-HEM-025.note: Familiar B12 absorption steps; Crohn ileitis, Diphyllobothrium and metformin are common alternates.

PLX-HEM-027.note: Generic contexts tied together by phenytoin; methotrexate or trimethoprim are equally expected members.

PLX-HEM-028.note: Normal MMA is the discriminating tile; the rest are shared megaloblastic findings.

PLX-HEM-030.note: Requires separating DBA from Fanconi anemia and transient erythroblastopenia; triphalangeal thumbs is the key clue.

PLX-HEM-032.note: Standard platelet-type bleeding disorders; uremic platelet dysfunction and aspirin also fit.

PLX-HEM-033.note: TPO-receptor agonists anchor ITP; splenectomy and anti-D are common expected alternates.

PLX-HEM-035.note: The HUS triad plus bloody diarrhea prodrome is recognized instantly.

PLX-HEM-036.note: Reduced vWF activity restates the title, and the hedged qualifiers make two tiles vague.

revision.why: Ristocetin cofactor activity is the standard vWF functional assay without echoing the title; prolonged bleeding time is a classic, definite primary-hemostasis clue and replaces the hedged platelet-count tile.
revision.changes: Reduced vWF activity -> Reduced ristocetin cofactor activity; Often normal platelet count -> Prolonged bleeding time

PLX-HEM-037.note: The standard inherited thrombophilia list; protein S deficiency fits equally and will be expected.

PLX-HEM-038.note: Lupus anticoagulant and anticardiolipin quickly suggest APS; the false-positive VDRL needs brief recall.

PLX-HEM-039.note: Classic extrinsic-pathway causes; quick for most.

PLX-HEM-040.note: Low fibrinogen with high D-dimer identifies DIC quickly.

PLX-HEM-041.note: The 'Young Liver Synthesizes Blood' mnemonic sequence, with Fetal repeated in two tiles.

revision.why: Removes the repeated Fetal prefix; the title already establishes developmental context.
revision.changes: Fetal liver -> Liver; Fetal spleen -> Spleen

PLX-HEM-043.note: The PSaMMoma mnemonic set is memorized as a unit.

PLX-HEM-044.note: Must be separated from pyrimidine analogues with similar -abine/-ribine names; 6-thioguanine also fits.

PLX-HEM-045.note: Three tiles end in -abine, and 5-FU with its prodrug capecitabine is an easy pair.

revision.why: Capecitabine is simply the 5-FU prodrug and adds a third -abine suffix; azacitidine is a definite pyrimidine (cytidine) analogue used for MDS/AML.

PLX-HEM-047.note: All four are -mab antibodies; the challenge is excluding CTLA-4 (ipilimumab), and avelumab/cemiplimab also fit.

PLX-HEM-048.note: Requires recall of alkylator/platinum mechanism; melphalan, nitrosoureas and other platinums also fit.

PLX-HEM-049.note: Familiar rescue/protectant pairings; rasburicase or glucarpidase could be expected.

PLX-HEM-050.note: Many oncogenic kinases (EGFR, ALK, KIT) fit equally, so the set feels arbitrary; BCR-ABL1, BRAF and JAK2 also recur as tiles in 052, 056 and 063.

PLX-HEM-051.note: All tiles end in lymphoma; ALCL t(2;5) is an equally valid member.

PLX-HEM-052.note: BCR-ABL1 gives CML away and duplicates the BCR-ABL1 tile in PLX-HEM-050.

revision.why: Removes the BCR-ABL1 giveaway and the cross-group duplicate tile; splenomegaly is a certain, common CML finding, and the remaining set still points to CML through reasoning.

PLX-HEM-053.note: t(15;17) and PML-RARA are the same lesion stated twice, both instant giveaways.

revision.why: PML-RARA duplicates t(15;17); DIC at presentation is a certain, clinically important APL association that requires recall.

PLX-HEM-054.note: Reed-Sternberg plus CD15/CD30 is a memorized triad.

revision.why: Breaks the CD15/CD30 pair that sorts mechanically; bimodal age distribution is a certain classical Hodgkin feature requiring recall.

PLX-HEM-055.note: Endemic jaw vs sporadic abdominal involvement is a memorized pair sharing the word involvement.

revision.why: Removes the paired endemic/sporadic involvement tiles; EBV association (especially endemic form) is certain.

PLX-HEM-056.note: Hair-like projections echoes the title; BRAF also duplicates a tile in PLX-HEM-050.

revision.why: Removes the title-echoing tile; massive splenomegaly is a classic, certain hairy-cell clue (shared with CML/myelofibrosis, which adds discrimination).

PLX-HEM-057.note: Smudge cells and Richter transformation are both CLL giveaways.

revision.why: Smudge cells is the reflex giveaway; CD5-positive B cells is certain for CLL and forces discrimination from mantle cell lymphoma.

PLX-HEM-058.note: Cerebriform nuclei with erythroderma points quickly to Sezary syndrome.

PLX-HEM-059.note: HTLV-1 anchors the group; hypercalcemia and lytic lesions usefully overlap with myeloma.

PLX-HEM-060.note: The CRAB mnemonic is memorized as a unit; inherent to the connection.

PLX-HEM-061.note: Requires linking detection findings and complications to monoclonal light chains; free-light-chain repeats the title.

revision.why: Abnormal kappa/lambda ratio is the standard way to express an abnormal serum free light-chain assay and removes the title echo.
revision.changes: Abnormal serum free-light-chain assay -> Abnormal kappa/lambda ratio

PLX-HEM-062.note: Monoclonal IgM with hyperviscosity is a well-known Waldenstrom pairing.

PLX-HEM-063.note: JAK2 gives PV away quickly and duplicates the JAK2 tile in PLX-HEM-050.

revision.why: Removes the JAK2 giveaway and cross-group duplicate; erythromelalgia is a certain, characteristic PV (and ET) symptom.

PLX-HEM-064.note: Teardrop cells plus 'bone marrow fibrosis' make it quick; the fibrosis tile restates the title.

revision.why: 'Bone marrow fibrosis' is the diagnosis restated; a dry tap is the classic, certain marrow clue and requires a step of reasoning.
revision.changes: Tile 3 'Bone marrow fibrosis' -> 'Dry tap on aspiration'.

PLX-HEM-065.note: The classic TLS quartet is a memorized set and the Hyper-/Hypo- format groups the electrolyte tiles instantly.

IMM-001.note: Spleen and lymph nodes are the textbook secondary lymphoid organs; MALT/appendix also fit.

revision.why: Lymph nodes are the most obvious member; the appendix is certainly gut-associated secondary lymphoid tissue and makes the set less automatic.

IMM-002.note: Delayed cord separation is a classic instant clue, and 'leukocyte adhesion' in tile 4 repeats the title.

revision.why: Tile 4 restates the disease name; marked neutrophilia (neutrophils cannot leave vessels) is a certain, classic LAD-1 finding that requires mechanistic thought.

IMM-003.note: Partial albinism with giant granules is an instant Chediak-Higashi pattern; LYST adds a further giveaway.

IMM-004.note: All four end in '-GF', so they sort as growth factors without reasoning.

IMM-005.note: All IL- tiles require telling Th2 from Th1/Th17/Treg sets, but IL-10 is now regarded as a broadly regulatory cytokine rather than specifically Th2.

IMM-006.note: CD8 and beta-2 microglobulin make class I quick; 'presentation' repeats the title.

revision.title: MHC class I features
revision.why: Removes the title word 'presentation' that also appears in tile 3; membership unchanged.
revision.changes: Title 'MHC class I presentation clues' -> 'MHC class I features'.

IMM-007.note: 'HLA-DP / DQ / DR' and CD4 give class II instantly; 'presentation' repeats the title.

revision.title: MHC class II features
revision.why: Removes the title word 'presentation' that also appears in tile 4; membership unchanged.
revision.changes: Title 'MHC class II presentation clues' -> 'MHC class II features'.

IMM-008.note: FOXP3 with CD25 is a well-known Treg signature; IL-10/TGF-beta overlap other groups and add some discrimination.

IMM-009.note: CD19/CD20/CD21 read as a consecutive B-cell marker series.

revision.why: Breaks the CD19-20-21 run; surface IgD is certainly expressed on mature naive B cells and is a more discriminating member.
revision.changes: Tile 2 'CD20' -> 'Surface IgD'; tile order now CD19, CD21, Surface IgD, MHC class II.

IMM-010.note: Requires recognizing the components of T-dependent B-cell help; tiles overlap MHC II and hyper-IgM groups.

IMM-011.note: Placental transfer and most abundant serum antibody quickly identify IgG.

IMM-014.note: Mast cells, allergen crosslinking and type I hypersensitivity point to IgE immediately.

IMM-015.note: C6-C9 is a numbered series recognised as the membrane attack complex.

IMM-016.note: Bradykinin plus low C4 is a well-known HAE pairing, though tiles alone take a moment.

IMM-018.note: A memorized live-vaccine list; Sabin polio, intranasal influenza and smallpox also fit.

IMM-019.note: Must separate protein-antigen vaccines from live and inactivated whole-virus groups.

IMM-020.note: Many non-live viral vaccines (influenza, rabies) fit; 'Source-listed' is meaningless to players.

revision.title: Non-live viral vaccines
revision.why: 'Source-listed' is an authoring artefact; the real relationship is non-live viral vaccine, membership unchanged.
revision.changes: Title 'Source-listed non-live viral vaccines' -> 'Non-live viral vaccines'.

IMM-021.note: TRECs and absent thymic shadow are well-known SCID clues, with some overlap with DiGeorge.

revision.why: BTK is a direct giveaway; chronic enteroviral meningoencephalitis is a classic, certain XLA complication that requires clinical recall.

IMM-023.note: Thymic hypoplasia with hypocalcemia is the instant DiGeorge pairing; low PTH and hypocalcemia are near-redundant.

IMM-024.note: 'IgA' appears in three tiles and in the title, so the group sorts by word.

tiles: Low IgA with preserved IgG / IgM
revision.why: Removes one of three repeated 'IgA' stems while keeping the same recognized association.

IMM-025.note: 'Defective CD40 ligand' repeats the title and gives the answer.

revision.why: Removes the title-word giveaway; opportunistic Pneumocystis pneumonia is a classic feature of CD40L deficiency that distinguishes it from AID-type hyper-IgM.

IMM-026.note: 'STAT3 mutation' repeats the title; cold abscesses plus high IgE is already classic.

revision.why: Removes the title-word giveaway; retained primary teeth is a classic, certain feature of STAT3 hyper-IgE (Job) syndrome.

IMM-027.note: 'WAS protein' names the syndrome; eczema with small platelets is already instant.

tiles: Low IgM with high IgA / IgE
revision.why: Removes the name giveaway; low IgM with elevated IgA and IgE is the classic, certain WAS immunoglobulin pattern.
revision.changes: Tile 1 'WAS protein defect' -> 'Low IgM with high IgA / IgE'.

IMM-028.note: Requires recalling inheritance; X-linked CGD and IL2RG SCID also fit.

IMM-029.note: Three tiles contain 'hemolytic'; Goodpasture, myasthenia, Graves and pemphigus are other well-known type II examples.

IMM-030.note: Classic type III list; 'immune-complex' appears in both the title and tile 4.

revision.title: Classic type III hypersensitivity examples
revision.why: Removes the 'immune-complex' word shared with tile 4 using the standard equivalent term; membership unchanged.
revision.changes: Title 'Classic immune-complex hypersensitivity examples' -> 'Classic type III hypersensitivity examples'.

IMM-031.note: Contact dermatitis plus PPD are the stock type IV examples.

IMM-034.note: 'Pulmonary' recurs in three tiles and 'after transfusion' names the setting; requires only separating from TACO.

IMM-035.note: Preformed antibodies with minutes-scale onset is a classic hyperacute signature; 'graft' repeats the title.

revision.why: Removes the repeated title word 'graft' from two tiles without changing meaning.
revision.changes: Tile 2 'Minutes after graft reperfusion' -> 'Onset within minutes of reperfusion'; tile 3 'Graft microvascular thrombosis' -> 'Microvascular thrombosis'.

IMM-036.note: 'Graft arteriosclerosis' is the standard term and gives the answer; 'graft' also recurs in tile 4.

revision.why: Removes the second repeated 'graft' while keeping the standard term in tile 1.

IMM-037.note: 'Donor T-cell attack on host' restates the disease; skin, gut, liver is the classic triad.

IMM-038.note: Transplant drugs sharing an IL-2 axis require mechanism knowledge; mycophenolate/azathioprine are tempting non-members.

IMM-039.note: Well-known steroid toxicities; many others (cataracts, myopathy, infection) fit equally.

IMM-040.note: All four share the '-limumab/-zumab' stem and form the anti-TNF list; etanercept is the expected missing member.

revision.why: Etanercept is a certain anti-TNF biologic that breaks the all '-mab' pattern and removes the missing-member risk.

MICRO-001.note: Requires knowing each toxin's mechanism and discriminating from ETEC ST and lethal factor.

MICRO-002.note: Requires mechanism recall, but the two Shiga tiles pair themselves.

MICRO-003.note: Requires recalling phage-encoded toxins and separating from mechanism groups; botulinum toxin (ABCD'S) also fits.

MICRO-004.note: The SHiN mnemonic makes this an instant list, and two Neisseria tiles pair themselves.

MICRO-005.note: Four Clostridium/Clostridioides names sort immediately by genus.

MICRO-006.note: A memorized urease list (CHUNKS PPP); Ureaplasma, Nocardia and Cryptococcus are equally expected members.

MICRO-008.note: HACEK now usually grows in modern cultures and Tropheryma also fits; 'species' recurs in three tiles.

revision.why: Removes the repeated 'species' suffix; genus names alone are standard and the meaning is unchanged.

MICRO-009.note: A standard atypical-pneumonia list; Coxiella also fits and the two Chlamydia tiles pair.

MICRO-010.note: Listeria and Brucella are classic; EHEC, M. bovis and Coxiella also share the raw-dairy route.

MICRO-012.note: Trismus, risus sardonicus and opisthotonos are the stock tetanus triad.

MICRO-013.note: 'Descending flaccid paralysis' is the key giveaway, though the autonomic tiles need cholinergic reasoning.

MICRO-014.note: 'Positive Legionella urine antigen' names the organism outright.

revision.why: Removes the organism name; growth on buffered charcoal yeast extract agar is a certain, classic Legionella clue that requires recall.
revision.changes: Tile 4 'Positive Legionella urine antigen' -> 'Growth on BCYE agar'.

MICRO-015.note: Classic Pseudomonas exposure buzzwords; quick for most but each tile has a plausible non-pseudomonal decoy.

MICRO-016.note: Hutchinson teeth instantly signals congenital syphilis; interstitial keratitis, mulberry molars and Clutton joints are equally expected members.

revision.why: Hutchinson teeth is the single giveaway tile; Clutton joints (painless bilateral knee effusions) are a definite late congenital syphilis stigma and leave saddle nose and saber shins with real decoys (GPA, Paget).

MICRO-017.note: Clue cells and whiff test are instant BV buzzwords; fixed criteria set cannot be altered without losing precision.

MICRO-018.note: Standard endemic mycoses list; Talaromyces marneffei is a fair alternate, and three tiles overlap MICRO-019.

MICRO-019.note: Requires excluding Coccidioides (spherules in tissue); Talaromyces marneffei also forms yeast in tissue and could be expected.
