revision.why: Current wording ('tissue forms ... that become yeast') is awkward; the new title states the same criterion directly.

MICRO-020.note: 'Cryptococcal antigen' names the organism, and India ink/mucicarmine are instant buzzwords.

revision.why: Removes the tile that names the organism; markedly elevated CSF opening pressure is a definite, clinically important feature of cryptococcal meningitis.
revision.changes: Replace 'Positive cryptococcal antigen' with 'High CSF opening pressure'.

MICRO-021.note: Septate acute-angle hyphae is the textbook Aspergillus descriptor and gives the group away.

revision.why: The halo sign (nodule with surrounding ground-glass) is a definite classic imaging clue of angioinvasive pulmonary aspergillosis and is less of a buzzword than the hyphae description.
revision.changes: Replace 'Septate acute-angle branching hyphae' with 'CT halo sign'.

MICRO-022.note: Asthma, IgE and eosinophilia overlap EGPA and allergic asthma; bronchiectasis tips it to ABPA.

MICRO-025.note: CD4 under 200 plus TMP-SMX prophylaxis points quickly to PCP, though toxoplasmosis is a brief decoy.

MICRO-026.note: Flask-shaped ulcers and anchovy paste are instant Entamoeba buzzwords; no clean less-obvious substitute without loosening precision.

MICRO-027.note: Camping water plus steatorrhea is a well-known Giardia pairing; IgA deficiency adds a modest reasoning step.

MICRO-028.note: Acid-fast oocysts with HIV diarrhea points to Cryptosporidium, but Cystoisospora and Cyclospora are fair look-alikes.

MICRO-030.note: Four 'Plasmodium' tiles sort themselves; P. knowlesi is a recognized fifth human species.

MICRO-031.note: Maltese cross is a giveaway, but Ixodes and asplenia carry good Lyme and encapsulated-organism decoys.

MICRO-032.note: Sandfly plus macrophage amastigotes identifies kala-azar quickly; hepatosplenomegaly and pancytopenia are nonspecific.

MICRO-033.note: Loeffler-syndrome worms; Toxocara larvae also migrate through lung and appear in MICRO-034, so discrimination is needed.

MICRO-034.note: Requires separating egg ingestion from skin-penetrating larvae; Ascaris overlaps MICRO-033 deliberately.

MICRO-035.note: Two Taenia tiles pair up instantly; Anisakis (fish larvae) and Clonorchis (fish metacercariae) also fit.

revision.why: Removes the paired Taenia giveaway; Anisakis is definitively acquired by eating raw fish containing larvae and is a common expected member.

MICRO-036.note: 'Hepatic hydatid cyst' repeats the title and dog-sheep cycle is an instant giveaway.

revision.why: Removes the title word; daughter cysts within a hepatic cyst are a definite characteristic finding of cystic echinococcosis.
revision.changes: Replace 'Hepatic hydatid cyst' with 'Liver cyst with daughter cysts'.

MICRO-037.note: Flukes plus tapeworms maps quickly to praziquantel; paragonimiasis also fits, while fascioliasis is a good near miss (triclabendazole).

MICRO-038.note: Well-known ivermectin indications; permethrin is a fair alternate thought for scabies and lice.

MICRO-039.note: Dengue/Zika/chikungunya/yellow fever is a well-drilled Aedes set and every tile ends in 'virus'.

MICRO-040.note: BOAR mnemonic makes this instant; the Bunyavirales tile is wordy and its parenthetical is distracting.

revision.why: The parenthetical taxonomy note makes the tile long and odd-looking; 'Bunyavirales' alone is the current standard name with the same meaning.

MICRO-041.note: Recognizable paramyxo/pneumovirus set; human metapneumovirus also uses an F protein and fits.

MICRO-042.note: Classic 'PAPP' naked DNA virus mnemonic; instant for Step 1 students.

MICRO-044.note: Quick HPV association; vulva and vagina are equally valid squamous sites players may expect.

MICRO-045.note: 'EBV-positive' in a tile names the link outright.

revision.why: Removes the tile that names the virus; PTLD is a definite, classic EBV-driven malignancy in immunosuppressed transplant recipients.
revision.changes: Replace 'EBV-positive Hodgkin lymphoma' with 'Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder'.

MICRO-046.note: Linear esophageal ulcers and post-transplant pneumonitis steer to CMV, with HSV and Candida as fair decoys.

MICRO-047.note: Periventricular calcification is the CMV tell; other tiles overlap toxoplasmosis and rubella.

MICRO-048.note: PDA, cataracts and deafness form the classic congenital rubella triad, so the group is instant.

revision.why: Breaking the memorized triad forces recall; salt-and-pepper retinopathy is a definite classic congenital rubella finding.

MICRO-049.note: Erythema infectiosum names parvovirus B19 outright; other tiles follow instantly.

revision.why: Erythema infectiosum is the instant giveaway; papular-purpuric gloves-and-socks syndrome is a definite, well-described parvovirus B19 syndrome.

MICRO-050.note: Well-known HCV extrahepatic list; lichen planus is the least automatic member.

MICRO-051.note: Orchitis plus pancreatitis is the classic mumps pairing.

MICRO-052.note: Three tiles contain 'pox', so the poxvirus group sorts itself; no non-obscure substitute (e.g. orf) is a clear improvement.

MICRO-053.note: Janeway/Osler/Roth/splinter is the memorized endocarditis set; conjunctival petechiae is an equally classic member.

revision.why: Janeway lesions are the most endocarditis-specific giveaway; conjunctival petechiae are a definite classic peripheral sign of infective endocarditis, and the remaining tiles keep decoys (leukemia, trauma).

MICRO-054.note: All four end in '-cillin' and are the memorized antistaphylococcal penicillin list.

MICRO-056.note: The 'cef-' prefix groups them, but placing each in the correct generation versus cefepime, cefazolin or cefuroxime takes recall.

MICRO-057.note: Mnemonic-driven 50S list; one class tile among single drugs is a format tell, and streptogramins also fit.

revision.why: Replaces the drug-class tile with a single macrolide so all four tiles are the same kind of item; erythromycin certainly binds the 50S subunit.

MICRO-061.note: All tiles begin with 'Rif-', echoing the title's 'Rifamycins'.

MICRO-062.note: RIPE is an instant mnemonic set, and the title acronym spells the tiles.

MICRO-063.note: All end in '-conazole'; isavuconazole and ketoconazole fit equally.

MICRO-065.note: All end in '-tegravir'; cabotegravir is an equally valid member.

MICRO-066.note: Mixed suffixes require genuine class recall; etravirine is an equally valid member.

MICRO-067.note: Players will expect tenofovir, which is excluded only on the nucleoside-vs-nucleotide technicality.

MICRO-069.note: All four end in '-asvir', so the group sorts on suffix alone.

MICRO-070.note: All four end in -previr, which names the NS3/4A class outright; voxilaprevir, boceprevir and telaprevir fit equally, and the suffix is intrinsic so no fix exists without abandoning the class.

MSK-001.note: SITS is one of the most familiar closed anatomic sets; any three tiles reveal the fourth.

MSK-002.note: The PAIR mnemonic set; three tiles end in arthritis/spondyloarthritis and tile 4 repeats the title word, and since the set is closed a rewording would only worsen the arthritis stem.

MSK-003.note: Well-known enteric reactive arthritis four, but players must separate it from the overlapping invasive/bloody diarrhea organism lists.

MSK-004.note: Classic hyperuricemia list; two diuretic tiles share a stem, and pyrazinamide, a staple of the same list, is a likely expected member.

revision.why: Two 'diuretics' tiles pair off on wording; pyrazinamide certainly raises serum urate (inhibits renal urate excretion) and is the member players most expect.

MSK-005.note: The LOSS mnemonic maps one-to-one onto these tiles, so any student sorts them instantly; standard terms leave no meaningful rewording.

revision.why: Removes the redundant optical descriptor and adds a classic, certain CPPD association that requires recall rather than repeating crystal optics.
revision.changes: Replace 'Blue when aligned parallel to the compensator' with 'Hemochromatosis'; title broadened from arthritis to deposition disease so an associated condition fits.

MSK-007.note: Players must reason from defective osteoclast resorption to marrow crowding and foraminal narrowing; pancytopenia plus EMH tempts toward myelofibrosis.

MSK-009.note: Increasing hat size cues Paget quickly, though acromegaly is a reasonable competitor and the other tiles each have broader associations.

MSK-010.note: Standard csDMARD quartet that most students recognize quickly, though each drug has strong non-RA associations.

MSK-011.note: Hydralazine plus procainamide (SHIPP/HIPP mnemonic) gives the group away at once.

revision.why: Procainamide is the single most cued drug-induced lupus agent; minocycline is a well-established, certain cause that requires genuine recall and tempts toward other categories (tetracyclines, hyperpigmentation).

MSK-012.note: Congenital AV block points to anti-Ro, but rash, cytopenias and transaminitis also fit congenital TORCH infection, so players must discriminate.

MSK-013.note: Dry eyes plus dry mouth is instant Sjogren, and keratoconjunctivitis sicca and reduced Schirmer production are essentially the same clue twice.

revision.why: Removes the redundant dry-eye test and adds a certain, classic extraglandular Sjogren association that demands recall and tempts toward renal categories.
revision.changes: Replace 'Reduced Schirmer tear production' with 'Distal (type 1) RTA'; title broadened from diagnostic clues to clues.

MSK-015.note: Heliotrope rash and Gottron papules are pathognomonic textbook cues, and no less obvious member is both certain and not covered by an antisynthetase overlap.

MSK-017.note: Four letters of CREST; the mnemonic makes the group and its missing E immediate.

revision.why: Breaks the CREST letter pattern with the certain, characteristic serologic marker of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis.

MSK-018.note: Bilateral hilar adenopathy, noncaseating granulomas and elevated ACE form the textbook sarcoid triad.

revision.why: Elevated ACE is a single-disease giveaway; hypercalcemia (granuloma 1-alpha-hydroxylase activity) is a certain sarcoid association that tempts toward hyperparathyroidism and malignancy categories.

MSK-019.note: A well-known osteosarcoma risk list; Paget plus retinoblastoma makes it quick for most students.

MSK-020.note: Onion-skin periosteal reaction and EWSR1-FLI1 each name Ewing outright; the likely substitutes (CD99, t(11;22)) are just as obvious.

MSK-021.note: Tile 4 repeats 'giant-cell' from the title, and temporal headache plus jaw claudication already identifies GCA.

revision.why: Removes the title leak; scalp tenderness is a certain cranial GCA symptom that keeps the set clinical and consistent.
revision.changes: Replace 'Temporal artery giant-cell inflammation' with 'Scalp tenderness'.

MSK-022.note: PR3-ANCA (c-ANCA) is the board giveaway for GPA, so the rest need no discrimination from MPA/EGPA.

MSK-024.note: Players sort these as ANA-positive connective tissue diseases without needing Raynaud, and dermatomyositis fits the Raynaud link just as well.

MSK-025.note: A standard First Aid ulnar injury list; the fracture/compression pairs are recognizable but take a moment's localization.

MSK-033.note: Players must reason that each raises pressure in a closed fascial compartment; the tiles share no surface cue.

tiles: Tension (superolateral) side of the femoral neck

NEPH-005.note: The standard four potassium-sparing diuretics, memorized as a unit.

NEPH-007.note: The textbook nephrotic tetrad; heavy proteinuria plus hypoalbuminemia names the syndrome.

revision.why: Heavy proteinuria is the defining giveaway; the hypercoagulable state (urinary antithrombin III loss, renal vein thrombosis risk) is a certain classic nephrotic feature that requires recall.

NEPH-008.note: A classic MCD pattern, but effacement and negative immunofluorescence force discrimination from FSGS.

NEPH-009.note: HIV, heroin and sickle cell are the textbook FSGS associations, while obesity is a very common secondary cause players may expect.

NEPH-010.note: Each tile has many glomerular and systemic associations; linking them to membranous takes genuine recall.

NEPH-011.note: Anti-PLA2R cues membranous, but subepithelial deposits and granular staining also fit PSGN (NEPH-012), so placement takes discrimination.

NEPH-012.note: 'Recent streptococcal infection' restates the title; with subepithelial humps the group is immediate.

revision.why: Removes the title leak; cola-colored urine is a certain classic PSGN presenting clue that also tempts toward IgA nephropathy, so players must discriminate.

NEPH-013.note: 'Can't see, can't pee, can't hear' plus basket-weave makes this instant, and no certain, less obvious substitute exists.

NEPH-016.note: Coffin-lid crystals and staghorn calculus are textbook struvite cues; the obvious substitutes (Proteus) are no harder.

NEPH-017.note: Players must reason through oxalate load and citrate inhibition; hypocitraturia is a urinary abnormality rather than an exposure, and hypercalciuria is a likely expected member.

revision.title: Calcium oxalate stone risk factors
revision.why: Hypocitraturia is not an exposure, so 'risk factors' accurately covers all four members.
revision.changes: Title 'Calcium oxalate stone risk exposures' to 'Calcium oxalate stone risk factors'.

NEPH-018.note: Exactly the SAAD mnemonic (Sickle cell, Analgesics, Acute pyelonephritis, Diabetes), so it is sorted instantly.

revision.why: Breaks the SAAD mnemonic; urinary tract obstruction is an established papillary necrosis cause (the O in POSTCARDS).

NEPH-019.note: Classic 'P' AIN drugs; cephalosporins, sulfonamides, diuretics and allopurinol fit equally well.

NEPH-020.note: Standard ATN toxin list; IV contrast and hemoglobin are equally expected members, myoglobin adds some reasoning.

NEPH-021.note: Four numeric above/below thresholds share a format and form the memorized prerenal table.

revision.why: Urine sodium below 20 duplicates FENa below 1%; a bland sediment with hyaline casts is the standard prerenal urinalysis and breaks the numeric format.
revision.changes: Urine sodium below 20 mEq/L -> Hyaline casts

NEPH-023.note: Well-known ADPKD list; connective tissue disorders (Marfan, Ehlers-Danlos) give some useful decoy pull.

NEPH-024.note: EPO plus PTHrP points quickly to RCC, though ACTH pulls toward small cell lung cancer.

NEPH-025.note: Classic bladder cancer risk list; phenacetin pulls toward papillary necrosis.

NEPH-026.note: Standard acetazolamide indication list; glaucoma and raised ICP overlap mannitol uses.

NEPH-027.note: Lay-level grouping of everyday actions that raise abdominal pressure; exercise or jumping fit equally; consider retiring.

NEPH-028.note: The paired distal/proximal RTA tiles give it away, and acetazolamide duplicates the proximal RTA mechanism.

revision.why: Removes the revealing RTA pair and the acetazolamide/proximal RTA overlap; pancreatic fistula causes bicarbonate loss and a normal anion gap acidosis (HARDASS member).
revision.changes: Proximal renal tubular acidosis -> Pancreatic fistula

NEPH-030.note: Needs phosphate reasoning; all four also cause hypocalcemia and three cause hyperkalemia, so keep those categories off the same board.

NEPH-031.note: KW nodules are a form of mesangial expansion and foot-process effacement is nonspecific, while classic arteriolar hyalinosis is missing.

revision.title: Diabetic nephropathy histologic findings
revision.why: Efferent (as well as afferent) arteriolar hyalinosis is a characteristic, relatively specific diabetic lesion scored in the RPS classification, replacing the nonspecific effacement tile; the title is widened to histology to include the vascular pole.
revision.changes: Podocyte foot-process effacement -> Efferent arteriolar hyalinosis; title broadened

NEU-001.note: The four eponymous mechanoreceptors are a closed memorized set; no fair less obvious member exists, so consider retiring.

NEU-002.note: Textbook UMN list, and spasticity is a subtype of hypertonia, so two tiles are redundant.

revision.why: Replaces the hypertonia tile, which duplicates spasticity, with pronator drift, a standard sensitive UMN exam sign.

NEU-003.note: Textbook LMN list, recognized instantly, especially next to the UMN set.

revision.title: Lower motor neuron lesion findings
revision.why: Fibrillation potentials are the standard electrodiagnostic sign of LMN denervation, which takes some reasoning; the title is widened from examination signs to findings to fit.
revision.changes: Hypotonia -> Fibrillation potentials on EMG; title adjusted

NEU-004.note: All end in '-spinal tract'; the only challenge is excluding corticospinal and ascending tracts, and the names cannot be reworded.

NEU-005.note: Rule of 4 (motor nuclei that divide into 12 are medial) is well known; players may expect the accessory nerve as a 'pure motor' member.

NEU-006.note: These are the rule-of-4 '4 M's', two tiles contain 'medial' from the title, and tile 4 is a collective item that overlaps NEU-005.

revision.why: A specific medial motor nucleus replaces the vague collective tile and reduces the mnemonic feel; the hypoglossal nucleus is certainly paramedian.
revision.changes: Somatic motor cranial nerve nuclei -> Hypoglossal nucleus

NEU-007.note: These are the rule-of-4 lateral '4 S's', and three tiles begin with 'Spin-'.

NEU-008.note: 'Prefrontal' and 'Frontal eye fields' echo the title, and premotor cortex and the supplementary motor area fit equally.

revision.why: Removes one title-leaking tile; the supplementary motor area is certainly frontal (medial area 6).

NEU-009.note: Ipsilateral/contralateral plus 'below lesion' wording gives it away, and the laterality cannot be removed without changing meaning.

NEU-011.note: Uhthoff and bilateral INO are taught almost only as MS clues.

revision.why: Trigeminal neuralgia in a young adult is an established MS clue but is usually idiopathic, so it needs reasoning, unlike the MS-only Uhthoff tile.

NEU-012.note: Dawson fingers are a subtype of periventricular lesions, so tiles 1 and 2 overlap, and Dawson fingers gives the group away.

revision.why: Removes the tile 1/2 overlap; delayed VEP latency is a standard MS investigation finding showing subclinical optic nerve demyelination.
revision.changes: Periventricular white matter lesions -> Delayed visual evoked potentials

NEU-013.note: JC virus and natalizumab point to PML at once; the other two tiles are decent decoys toward MS.

NEU-014.note: Benzodiazepines and barbiturates point straight to GABA-A, and propofol, ethanol, zolpidem and etomidate fit equally.

NEU-015.note: Two '-stigmine' names give it away, and neostigmine, rivastigmine and galantamine are equally expected.

NEU-016.note: Generic oculobulbar weakness that is not specific to MG (botulism, brainstem stroke); dysphonia and fatigable chewing fit equally.

NEU-017.note: The VGCC antibody tile names the disease; SCLC and hyporeflexia are fair decoys.

NEU-018.note: 'Down-and-out' is the iconic CN III phrase and tiles 3 and 4 overlap.

revision.why: Loss of accommodation (parasympathetic supply to the ciliary muscle) is a certain feature of a complete pupil-involving CN III palsy and replaces both the catchphrase and the redundancy.
revision.changes: Down-and-out resting eye -> Loss of accommodation

NEU-020.note: Familiar CN VII branch list; useful contrast with the CN IX posterior-taste tile.

NEU-021.note: Stylopharyngeus and posterior-third taste are recognizable CN IX clues; the gag tile contrasts well with CN X.

NEU-022.note: Uvula deviation identifies CN X; deciding afferent versus efferent gag against CN IX adds discrimination.

NEU-023.note: These are the consecutive post-chiasmal visual pathway stations, so the only task is excluding the optic nerve and chiasm.

revision.why: A Meyer loop lesion causes a contralateral homonymous superior quadrantanopia, so it is certainly a retrochiasmal homonymous site and it breaks the obvious pathway series.

NEU-024.note: Tile 4 is an awkward near-duplicate of cerumen impaction that needs a 'non-cerumen' qualifier.

revision.why: TM perforation is a standard, unambiguous conductive cause and replaces the near-duplicate canal-mass tile.
revision.changes: Obstructing external canal mass (non-cerumen) -> Tympanic membrane perforation

NEU-025.note: Aminoglycoside ototoxicity and congenital CMV fit equally, and Meniere disease and vestibular schwannoma also appear in NEU-026.

NEU-026.note: Vestibular schwannoma rarely causes true vertigo, labyrinthitis is the expected missing member, and two tiles duplicate NEU-025.

revision.why: Labyrinthitis is an unequivocal peripheral vertigo cause; this removes the weak schwannoma member and one overlap with NEU-025.

NEU-027.note: Dix-Hallpike plus Epley plus positional vertigo is instantly BPPV.

revision.why: Torsional upbeating nystagmus is the defining Dix-Hallpike finding in posterior-canal BPPV and asks for more knowledge than 'positional vertigo'.
revision.changes: Brief position-triggered vertigo -> Torsional upbeating nystagmus

NEU-028.note: Each tile alone fits other tumors (neuroblastoma, pilocytic astrocytoma, ependymoma), so the group must be told apart from look-alike tumors.

NEU-029.note: Rosenthal fibers is a strong clue, and 'piloid' echoes 'pilocytic' in the title.

revision.why: Removes the 'piloid' echo of the title while keeping the standard histologic description.

NEU-030.note: Rathke pouch and wet keratin identify it quickly; the suprasellar tile adds pituitary adenoma pull.

NEU-031.note: Pseudopalisading necrosis identifies GBM; the butterfly and EGFR tiles have fair decoy pull toward CNS lymphoma and lung cancer.

NEU-032.note: Whorls plus arachnoid origin is a quick meningioma clue; psammoma bodies pull toward papillary thyroid and serous ovarian tumors.

NEU-033.note: The tiles fit any immunodeficiency-associated DLBCL (e.g., PTLD), with nothing CNS-specific, and 'Immunocompromised host' echoes the title.

revision.why: A periventricular enhancing mass is the classic PCNSL imaging clue; it anchors the set to the CNS and removes the echo of the title.

NEU-035.note: Reads as 'language areas'; the arcuate fasciculus and primary auditory cortex fit equally, and Broca area also appears in NEU-008.

NEU-036.note: Ipsilateral/contralateral pain-temperature wording and the '(nucleus ambiguus)' label point straight to Wallenberg.

revision.why: Drops the parenthetical nucleus label that does the localization for the player; the clinical meaning is the same.

NEU-038.note: Middle meningeal artery plus biconvex plus lucid interval is the iconic epidural triad.

revision.why: A pterion (temporal bone) fracture and confinement by sutures are certain epidural features that need one more inferential step than naming the artery and shape, and they pair as a discrimination with the subdural set.
revision.changes: Middle meningeal artery injury -> Pterion fracture; Biconvex (lentiform) CT collection -> Does not cross suture lines

NEU-039.note: Bridging veins plus crescent shape is the iconic subdural pair.

revision.why: Crossing suture lines is a certain subdural feature and creates a direct discrimination with the epidural 'does not cross suture lines' tile.
revision.changes: Crescent-shaped (concave) CT collection -> Crosses suture lines

NEU-040.note: 'Thunderclap headache' plus xanthochromia is instantly SAH.

tiles: Blood in basal cisterns on CT
revision.title: Subarachnoid hemorrhage associations
revision.why: Delayed vasospasm (classically days 3 to 14) is a certain SAH association that needs recall beyond the presenting headache; 'associations' in the title covers a complication.
revision.changes: Thunderclap headache -> Delayed cerebral vasospasm; title clues -> associations

NEU-041.note: Straight from the DANISH mnemonic; all four are textbook cerebellar signs.

revision.why: Scanning (ataxic) speech is a certain cerebellar sign that also pulls toward MS (Charcot triad), so it adds discrimination and removes one 'dys-' tile.

NEU-043.note: GAA repeat and frataxin name Friedreich ataxia outright; the two systemic tiles are carried by them.

NEU-045.note: Two tiles end in 'regulation' and the set is broad; thirst/water balance (ADH) fits the title just as well and may be expected.

NEU-046.note: Anosmia plus GnRH neuron migration is the textbook Kallmann pairing; instant for this audience.

NEU-047.note: Classic Parinaud signs; light-near dissociation and vertical gaze palsy also point to PSP/neurosyphilis, giving some discrimination.

revision.why: The slash inside tile 4 reads like two tiles and is clumsy; same meaning in standard terms.

NEU-049.note: The four named dopamine pathways form a memorized set and all end in 'pathway'.

revision.why: Removes the repeated 'pathway' stem; the bare names are the standard terms.

NEU-050.note: Plaques and tangles are instant; hyperphosphorylated tau duplicates the tangle tile.

revision.why: Tau is the constituent of tangles (redundant); Hirano bodies are a standard Alzheimer histologic finding (hippocampus) and add a distinct teaching point.

NEU-051.note: Donepezil and memantine are instantly linked to Alzheimer treatment; overlaps NEU-015.

NEU-053.note: Levodopa/carbidopa names Parkinson therapy at once; two tiles share 'inhibitors'.

NEU-054.note: Well-known DLB cluster; must be separated from Parkinson disease dementia and delirium.

NEU-055.note: Classic CJD tetrad; spongiform change and periodic sharp waves make it quick.

NEU-056.note: Standard reversible-dementia screen; normal pressure hydrocephalus is the obvious missing member, and the parentheticals give the link away.

revision.why: '(pseudodementia)' states the connection outright and 'Thyroid disease (hypothyroidism)' is redundant; meaning unchanged.

NEU-057.note: POUND-type features; quickly recognized as migraine.

NEU-058.note: Recognizable cluster autonomic signs; lacrimation/rhinorrhea also overlap the opioid-withdrawal and cholinergic sets in this chunk, so avoid sharing a board.

NEU-059.note: Familiar raised-ICP cluster; pulsatile tinnitus and CN VI palsy point quickly to IIH.

NEU-060.note: 3-Hz spike-and-wave and ethosuximide each identify absence seizures instantly.

NEU-061.note: All four end in 'seizure' and tile 2 repeats 'Generalized' from the title.

revision.why: Removes the repeated 'seizure' stem and the title word 'Generalized'; the title already specifies generalized onset.
revision.changes: Dropped 'seizure' from all tiles and 'Generalized' from tile 2.

NEU-062.note: Retraction bulbs plus rotational shear make diffuse axonal injury quick; location tiles add some ambiguity.

PHARM-001.note: All end in '-ation' and are the standard phase II list; glutathione conjugation fits equally.

PHARM-002.note: The classic inducer list from every mnemonic; instant for Step 1 students.

PHARM-003.note: Recognized inhibitors from the standard mnemonic, though each drug has a stronger primary association.

PHARM-004.note: 'HAVe 1 M&M' mnemonic; all four end in 'receptor'.

revision.why: Removes the repeated 'receptor' stem; bare receptor names are standard.

PHARM-005.note: Standard Gs list from the receptor mnemonic; all four end in 'receptor'.

revision.why: Removes the repeated 'receptor' stem; bare receptor names are standard.

PHARM-006.note: Familiar direct cholinergic agonists; carbachol fits equally.

PHARM-008.note: DUMBBELSS features; quick, though lacrimation and diarrhea also sit in the opioid-withdrawal set (PSY-010).

PHARM-009.note: Well-known anticholinergic toxidrome; dry skin separates it from sympathomimetic toxicity.

PHARM-010.note: Clonidine and guanfacine make it quick; methyldopa fits equally and tizanidine adds some challenge.

PHARM-011.note: All end in '-osin'; the suffix sorts them without reasoning, and every alternative member shares it.

PHARM-013.note: '-olol' shows beta blockers at once, but players must tell nonselective from beta-1-selective agents.

PHARM-014.note: All four share the '-afil' suffix; unavoidable for this class.

PHARM-017.note: Players must decide which catecholamines have beta-1 inotropy; dopamine (moderate dose) fits equally well.

PHARM-019.note: Recognizable toxic metals; copper (Wilson disease) is an equally valid member.

PSY-001.note: Straight from the SAASH mature-defense mnemonic; anticipation is a valid missing member.

PSY-002.note: The complete 2x2 operant grid with repeated words; sortable without reasoning, and wording cannot be changed without nonstandard terms.

PSY-003.note: The complete DSM Cluster B set with a shared 'personality disorder' stem.

PSY-004.note: 'Trauma-cue' in tile 2 points directly to PTSD; the four DSM clusters are well known.

PSY-005.note: Leaden paralysis and mood reactivity identify atypical depression quickly; rejection sensitivity is a valid fifth member.

PSY-006.note: Textbook positive-symptom list; two tiles share 'Disorganized'.

PSY-007.note: Classic narcolepsy tetrad; three tiles contain 'sleep'.

revision.why: Cuts the repeated 'sleep' stem to two tiles using the standard term with identical meaning.

PSY-008.note: Familiar bulimia/vomiting cluster; the 'Russell sign' label makes it quicker.

PSY-009.note: Lanugo plus amenorrhea gives it away; 'Nutritional deficiencies' is a broad category, not a discrete clinical clue.

revision.why: Sinus bradycardia is a standard, discrete clinical finding of anorexia-related undernutrition; the vague 'Nutritional deficiencies' tile is not a specific clue.

PSY-010.note: Yawning gives opioid withdrawal away quickly; lacrimation, rhinorrhea and diarrhea overlap NEU-058 and PHARM-008, so avoid sharing a board.

PSY-012.note: Best-known SSRIs; citalopram and escitalopram are an enantiomer pair, so one tile gives away the other.

revision.why: Escitalopram duplicates citalopram (S-enantiomer); paroxetine is certainly an SSRI and adds a distinct teaching point (most anticholinergic, discontinuation syndrome).

PSY-013.note: Venlafaxine/desvenlafaxine share a stem and duloxetine is well known; levomilnacipran is less familiar.

PSY-014.note: Two '-triptyline' and two '-pramine' tiles reveal the class at a glance.

revision.why: Nortriptyline repeats the '-triptyline' stem of amitriptyline (and is its metabolite); doxepin is certainly a TCA without the revealing suffix.

PSY-015.note: Benzodiazepines are obvious, but players must exclude the lorazepam-oxazepam-temazepam (LOT) group.

PSY-016.note: Three tiles end in '-barbital'; the class is obvious, and other barbiturates share the suffix.

PSY-017.note: Opioids are obvious; must separate from partial agonists, and oxycodone or oxymorphone fit equally well.

PSY-018.note: Typical antipsychotics are easy, but players must exclude low-potency agents like chlorpromazine and thioridazine.

PSY-019.note: Classic EPS quartet taught with antipsychotics; quickly recognized.

PSY-020.note: Oculogyric crisis points quickly to acute dystonia after antipsychotic or antiemetic exposure; the other tiles have broader associations.

PSY-021.note: Ebstein anomaly plus nephrogenic DI is a textbook lithium giveaway, and Ebstein is a fetal exposure effect mixed in with patient adverse effects.

revision.why: Ebstein anomaly is the instant lithium cue and belongs to a different exposure context (prenatal). Lithium-associated hyperparathyroidism with hypercalcemia is a well-established patient adverse effect.

PSY-022.note: Linezolid with meperidine is a well-known serotonin syndrome pairing, so the link comes quickly but needs recall.

PSY-023.note: These four tiles are the memorized NMS tetrad (FARM), and lead-pipe rigidity alone gives it away.

revision.why: The four tiles are the memorized NMS tetrad (FARM). A markedly elevated CK is a classic, defining NMS lab finding, and swapping it in for fever breaks the mnemonic without losing accuracy.

PSY-025.note: These are standard nonpharmacologic delirium measures and are recognized quickly by students; 'Visible' repeats in only two tiles.

REPRO-001.note: These four tiles spell the SEED mnemonic for Wolffian derivatives exactly.

revision.why: Swapping in the female mesonephric remnant breaks the SEED mnemonic and makes players think about the duct's fate in both sexes. A Gartner duct is certainly a mesonephric duct remnant.

REPRO-002.note: Only forebrain leptomeninges come from neural crest, so that tile needs an unstated exception.

revision.why: Leptomeninges are only partly neural crest-derived (forebrain only). Odontoblasts are an unambiguous neural crest derivative.

REPRO-004.note: Horseshoe kidney, coarctation, and cystic hygroma together are a classic instant Turner cluster.

REPRO-005.note: A 46,XY karyotype with breasts and no uterus quickly suggests CAIS; MRKH is a look-alike.

REPRO-007.note: Mole and choriocarcinoma point quickly to hCG; trisomy 21 is a screening-level association rather than reliable elevation.

REPRO-008.note: Students recognize these quickly as hemodynamic parameters; deciding the direction in pregnancy takes a little recall.

REPRO-009.note: These are familiar Potter-sequence causes; the link to fetal urine is easy to work out.

REPRO-010.note: These are classic polyhydramnios causes (impaired swallowing, GI obstruction, fetal polyuria) and are recognized readily.

REPRO-011.note: These four tiles are the memorized 4 Ts list (Tone, Trauma, Tissue, Thrombin).

revision.title: Causes of postpartum hemorrhage
revision.why: The generic category labels map one-to-one onto the 4 Ts mnemonic. Specific examples need recall, and each is certainly a cause of postpartum hemorrhage.
revision.changes: Replace 'Genital tract trauma' with 'Cervical laceration' and 'Coagulation disorder' with 'Disseminated intravascular coagulation'; retitle to 'Causes of postpartum hemorrhage'.

REPRO-012.note: These match the well-known mnemonic 'Hypertensive Moms Love Nifedipine', and there are few safe alternatives to swap in.

REPRO-013.note: Cocaine strongly cues abruption; the fibroid association is weak and inconsistent, while a very common risk factor (trauma) is missing.

revision.why: Evidence for uterine fibroids as a risk factor is weak and inconsistent. Abdominal trauma is a classic, certain precipitant of abruption.

REPRO-014.note: Telling complete from partial mole takes discrimination (p57 loss, androgenetic genome, diffuse rather than focal changes).

REPRO-015.note: 'Unopposed estrogen' and 'estrogen' appear in tiles, which gives away the shared mechanism.

revision.why: Two tiles repeat the title's wording. Obesity (peripheral aromatization) and granulosa cell tumor (an estrogen-secreting tumor) are certain, standard causes of prolonged unopposed estrogen exposure.
revision.changes: Replace 'Unopposed estrogen therapy' with 'Obesity' and 'Estrogen-secreting ovarian tumor' with 'Granulosa cell tumor'. Do not use this on the same board as REPRO-018.

REPRO-016.note: Dyschezia with cyclic pain and infertility points quickly to endometriosis.

REPRO-017.note: Dysgerminoma and yolk sac tumor are well-known germ cell tumors; the two teratomas make the group easy to spot.

REPRO-018.note: These are standard sex cord-stromal tumors that most students sort quickly.

REPRO-019.note: This is the familiar 'fewer ovulations' protective list; tubal ligation needs slightly more thought.

REPRO-020.note: Spironolactone, ketoconazole, and cimetidine are a classic gynecomastia list, and players may expect digoxin.

REPRO-021.note: The '-relin' suffix on three tiles gives the group away; this cannot be fixed by rewording, so use antagonists (degarelix, cetrorelix) as decoys.

REPRO-022.note: These are familiar contraceptive progestins; only two tiles share the '-gestrel' stem.

REPRO-023.note: Under US MEC, a history of DVT is Category 4 only when acute or when recurrence risk is higher; acute DVT/PE is unambiguously Category 4.

revision.why: 'Prior DVT' can be Category 3 with low recurrence risk, while acute DVT/PE is unambiguously Category 4 in US MEC 2024.
revision.changes: Replace 'Prior deep venous thrombosis' with 'Acute deep venous thrombosis'.

REPRO-024.note: Absent cremasteric reflex with a high-riding testis is the textbook torsion pair, and 'testicular' repeats the title.

revision.why: Removes the title word 'testicular' and shortens the long Doppler tile without changing meaning.
revision.changes: Change 'Sudden severe testicular pain' to 'Sudden severe scrotal pain' and 'Reduced or absent Doppler blood flow' to 'Reduced or absent Doppler flow'.

REPRO-025.note: The age split (STI pathogens vs enterics) is classic, but Pseudomonas is a less expected member; Klebsiella or Mycoplasma genitalium fit equally well.

PULM-001.note: This is the memorized pulmonary fibrosis drug list; methotrexate mainly causes hypersensitivity pneumonitis rather than chronic fibrosis.

revision.why: Methotrexate lung injury is predominantly hypersensitivity pneumonitis. Chronic nitrofurantoin use is a well-established cause of pulmonary fibrosis and is less often grouped with these drugs.

PULM-002.note: SIADH, ectopic ACTH, and Lambert-Eaton together are a quick small cell carcinoma cue.

PULM-003.note: This is the standard neuroendocrine marker panel; NSE is mainly a serum marker, and all four also stain carcinoid tumors.

PULM-004.note: This is a fixed, memorized sequence and the two 'hepatization' tiles give it away instantly; membership cannot change without breaking the series.

PULM-005.note: Four '-osis' occupational lung diseases are instantly grouped, and organic dusts (byssinosis, farmer's lung) also fit the title as written.

PULM-006.note: These are recognized quickly as neuromuscular weakness disorders; linking them to restrictive physiology takes a short step.

PULM-007.note: Players must reason about compliance rather than shared clinical features; 'restrictive' or 'diffuse infiltrates' are competing readings.

PULM-008.note: Three tiles start with 'Increased' and the set is the CADET right-shift mnemonic.

revision.why: Removes the repeated 'Increased' stem using standard equivalent terms.
revision.changes: Change 'Increased temperature' to 'Hyperthermia' and 'Increased carbon dioxide' to 'Hypercapnia'.

PULM-009.note: Three tiles start with 'Decreased'; the set is a straight mirror image of the right-shift list.

revision.why: Removes the 'Decreased' stem with standard terms, and replacing the mirror-image 2,3-BPG tile with fetal hemoglobin (a classic, certain left shift) makes it less mechanical.

PULM-010.note: These are recognized quickly as hypoxemia mechanisms; seeing that shunt is the excluded fifth takes a moment.

PULM-012.note: These are classic ARDS precipitants with broad other associations, so the link needs only brief recall.

PULM-013.note: The obstructive diseases are instantly recognizable (bronchiectasis is an expected missing member), and the title wrongly refers to 'the source'.

PULM-016.note: Keratin pearls and PTHrP hypercalcemia are the textbook squamous cell lung giveaways.

revision.why: Keratin pearls are the instant cue. Cavitation is a classic supportive feature of pulmonary squamous cell carcinoma (the lung cancer type most likely to cavitate) and needs more thought.

PULM-017.note: 'Asbestos' appears in two tiles and 'pleural' in three, which gives the group away immediately.

revision.why: Removes the title word and the repeated 'pleural' stem. Bronchogenic carcinoma is the most common asbestos-related malignancy, and lower-lobe interstitial fibrosis is the standard description of asbestosis.
revision.changes: Replace 'Benign asbestos pleural effusion' with 'Bronchogenic carcinoma'; reword 'Pleural mesothelioma' to 'Mesothelioma' and 'Asbestosis' to 'Lower-lobe interstitial fibrosis'.
